This shall include, but not limited to, housing subdivision projects, planned unit developments, mixed-use establishments, and the like." (ltalics and underscori ng supplied) The amended Ordinance is VAGUE and AMBIGUOUS. lt is not clear whether, in the development of green spaces, this shall be done within the allotted open space of the proponent, set back areas of home lots or sidewalk strips based on PD 957 or BP220 design standards, AS ENUMERATED or whether these set back areas of home lots or sidewalk strips based on PD 957 or BP220 design standards are all located WITHIN the proponent's allotted open space. It is also prejudicial to public interest and an exercise of tegislative power in ultra vires. This is manifested by the use of the modal verb "shall," connoting a mandatory requirement for the turnover of these green spaces to the homeowners association for proper maintenance. There is now the unwarranted burden of maintaining the green space, passed on to the homeowners association, which exceeds the requirement of P.D. 1216. Under P.D. 1216, only parks and playgrounds of the entire open space MAY be donated to the Homeownens associations. Without looking into the capability and willingness of the homeowners association to accept the responsibitity of maintaining the GREEN SPACE, the transfer of authority without any corresponding liability is inimical to the interest of the City and general populace. Questions may arise on who should shoulder or pay damage/s, should there be any, which may result from the negligence in the maintenance of green spaces. Definitely, the homeowners association cannot be compelled to assume the obligation to pay for the very simple reason that it is only acting as caretakers of these green spaces. Moreover, Art. 2189 of the New Civil Code of the Philippines is relevant and applicable on the matter, to quote: "Art. 2189. Provinces, cities and municipalities shall be liable for damages for the death of, or injuries suffered by, any person by reason of the defective condition of roads, streets, bridges, public buildings, and other public works under their control of supervision" Thus, the amended measure unnecessarily makes the City Government of Davao liable for the damages that may arise from the negligence of homeowners association or their representatives. ln such an event, the City will be forced to disburse public funds to cover the indemnity for damages resulting from acts of the homeowners associations or its representatives to which it has no control over. text: OBJECTIVE 1.1 The objective of this Memorandum of Agreement is for DOH and City Health OfficeReproductive Health and Wellness Centre (CHO-RHWC) under the CITY GOVERNMENT OF DAVAO to Enter into a partnership for the collaborative approach in the provision of services related to HIV and AIDS including access to antiretroviral drugs for people living with HIV; t.2 For CHO-RHWC to become one of the official DOH-designated satellite treatment hubs in the country that facilitates the provision of safe, comprehensive and compassionate care to HIV and AIDS patients;
title: AN ORDINANCE GRANTING LEGISLATIVE AUTHORITY TO THE CITY MAYOR TO ENTER. INTO AND SIGN, FOR AND IN BEHATF OF THE CITY GOVERNMENT OF DAVAO THE MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT TO BE ENTERED INTO BY AND BETWEEN THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH REGION XI AND THE CITY GOVERNMENT OF DAVAO, PERTAINING TO A PARTNERSHIP FOR A COTLABORATIVE APPROACH IN THE PROVISION OF SERVICES FOR THE EXPANSION OF THE R.EPRODUCTIVE HEALTH

text: GENERAL PROVISION 2.L CHO-RHWC shall establish a mechanism and create policies and guidelines for HIV and AIDS within its facility; 2.2 CHO-RHWC shall designate a specific area/office/clinic for the medical team where services can be provided to patients including but not limited to HIV counselling and testing, clinical management, patient monitoring and other care and support services to people living with HIV and their family; CHO-RHWC shall allocate a desktop computer or laptop to be used exclusively for recording and maintenance of database of patients accessing HIV services at the family; CHO-RHWC shall utilize the reporting/monitoring tools prescribed by the DOH-NEC and submit the same to the DOH on a monthly basis; CHO-RHWC through its pharmacist shall monitor the stock level of antiretroviral drugs provided by the DOH to prevent stock outs; CHO-RHWC shall be responsible in the disposal of unutilized drugs for HIV provided by the DOH; CHO-RHWC shall ensure that the necessary protective equipment such as gloves, goggles and gown, shall be made available to all health care workers directly involved in the provision of services to PLHIV and similarly exposed personnel at alltimes; CHO-RHWC shall employ appropriate measures for TB infection control within its premises; CHO-RHWC shall make available services for post-exposure management for any health care workers with occupational exposure needing appropriate intervention, including provision of antiretroviral drugs as post- exposure prophylaxis per recommendation of the HACT; CHO-RHWC shall be an accredited provider of the Phil Health Outpatient HIV and AIDS Treatment (OHAT) Package and implement the same in accordance with the Phil Health Circular No. 10 s. 2010; z.LL CHO-RHWC shall strictly adhere to the policies and guidelines of the DOH on matters pertaining to the implementation of HIV and AIDS program in the health care setting; Access of Antiretroviral Drugs: Any PLHIV in need of antiretroviral (ARV) drug upon the clinical evaluation of a trained physician in accordance with DOH Administrative Order (AO) 2014-0031or Policies and Guidelines on the Use of Antiretroviral Therapy Among People Living with Human lmmunodeficiency Virus (HlV) and HIV- exposed lnfants can access the said drugs at CHO-RHWC through the HACT. The PLHIV in need of ARV has to consult the HACT and will only be enrolled in antiretroviral therapy (ART) upon the recommendation of the HACT physician; 2.3 2.4 2.5 2.6 2.7 2.8 2.9 2.to lt ;'J -L A I 2.12 l 2.L3 Antiretroviral drugs shall be given for FREE subject to the availability of supply, which can be availed of anytime at the CHO-RHWC. The DOH, through the NASPCP, shall allocate these drugs to the CHO-RHWC based on the current number of patients; 2.14 The CHO-RHWC shall be responsible in reporting adverse drug reactions to DOH, NASPCP, and BFAD on monthly basis; 2.15 CHO-RHWC shall only give a maximum of three (3) month's supply of these drugs to PLHIV on ART for treatment and adherence monitoring by the physician; 2.16 Stored ARV at the CHO-RHWC can be used as post exposure prophylaxis only in case of occupational exposure of any healthcare workers, as per recommendation by the HACT. Antiretroviral drugs shall not be used as prophylaxis for any other forms of exposure; 2.77 CHO-RHWC shall store the antiretroviral drugs in a designated cabinet with lock and only a designated pharmacist/s or Nurse-in-charge shall have access to the key. Said pharmacist or Nurse-in-charge shall be responsible in the inventory of the drugs and preparation and submission of monthly stock inventory to the DOH through its Regional HIV and STI Coordinator; Hrv AND AIDS CORE TEAM (HAsr) 2.L8 The CHO-RHWC HACI Chairperson shall lead the team of health professionals in the diagnostic, treatment and management of PLHIV. Appropriate referral shall be made for services not available within its health facility. 2.19 The CHO-RHWC HACI shall ensure adherence to the provisions of RA 8504 and Davao City AIDS Ordinance. lt shall be responsible in ensuring confidentiality at all times. text: Delineation of Responsibilities PCF Recipient LGU shall: 1. Maintain a book of accounts for the PD Fund; 2. Issue an official receipt corresponding to the amount of PC fund subsidy received; 3. text: DECLARATION OF POUCY - It is the policy of the State, under the Local Government Code (Republic Act No. 7L60), that every local government unit shall exercise the powers expressly granted, those necessarily implied therefrom, as well as powers necessary, appropriate, or incidental for its efficient and effective governance, and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare. Fufthermore, local government units have the power and responsibility to ensure and suppoft, among other things, the maintenance of peace and order within their respective territorial jurisdictions. Likewise, consistent with the Human Security Act (Republic Act No. 9372), it is a declared policy of the State to protect life, libefi, and property from acts of terrorism, to condemn terrorism as inimical and dangerous to the national security of the country and to the welfare of the people, and to make terrorism a crime against the Filipino people, against humanity, and against the law of nations. sEcrIoN 4. PROHIBTTED Acrs - It shall be unlawful for any person to: a) Recruit another person to membership to terrorist groups, international or local, such as but not limited to ISIS, AL-QAEDA, and MAUTE GROUp; b) Be a member of terrorist groups, international or local and actively pafticipate in any unlawful activity; c) Manufacture, possession, and distribution of any reading materials, propaganda, paraphernalia, such as flag, clothing, stickers which are related to terrorist groups, international or local; sEcrIoN 5. DEFINTTIoN oF TERMS: For purposes of this ordinance: a) ISIS refers to the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria, a terrorist organization known for its human rights abuses, hate crimes, cruelty, massacre, rape, and forced religious conversions. b) AI-Qaeda means "The Base", "The Foundation" or "The Fundament,,. It refers to the militant Sunni Islamist multi-national organization founded in 19BB by Osama bin Laden, Abdullah Azzam and several other Arab volunteers who fought against the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in the 1980s. Al-Qaeda operates as network made up of Islamic extremists, Salafist jihadists. It has been designated as a terrorist group by the United Nations Security Council, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization Ord. No. 0230 -t7 (NATO), the European Union, the United States, Russia, India, various other countries. Al-Qaeda has mounted attacks on civilian military targets in various countries. d) TERRORIST GROUP - refers to any organization, association or group of persons or any entity owned or controlled by any terrorist or group that: (1) commits, or attempts to commit, terrorist acts by any means, directly or indirectly, unlawfully or willfully; (2) pafticipates as an accomplice in terrorist acts; (3) organizes or directs others to commit terrorist acts; (4) contributes to the commission of terrorist acts by a group of persons acting with common purpose of fufthering the terrorist acts where the contribution is made intentionally and with the aim of fufthering the terrorist acts or with the knowledge of the intention of the group to commit terrorist acts.

text: DECLARATION OF POUCY. The City recognizes that LGUs are primarily responsible for the implementation and enforcement of the provisions of Republic Act No. 9003, otherwise known as the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000. Through the Waste Analysis and Characterization Study (WACS) conducted in the city, biodegradable wastes constitute the bulk of waste generation and these come from public markets. In order for LGUs to fulfill one of its responsibilities to diveft solid wastes from being dumped to the Sanitary Landfill Facility, the DENR through the Environmental Management Bureau (EMB), launched the establishment and institutionalization of Solid waste Management System in public Markets.

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS. - For the purpose of this Ordinance, the following terms and phrases shall apply: 2.L. Protection Order - refers to an order issued under the Act for the purpose of preventing further acts of violence against a woman or her child specifled in SECTION 7 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) and granting other necessary relief. Barangay Protection Order (BPO)- refers to the protection order issued by the Punong Barangay (PB) or if the PB is unavailable, by a kagawad ordering the offender to desist from committing or threatening physical harm to the victim. It is effective for 15 days and is not extendible. a Permanent Protection Order (PPO) - refers to the protection order issued by the court after notice and hearing. Temporary Protection Order (TPO) - refers to the protection order issued by the court on the date of filing of the application after ex parte determination that such order should be issued. A couft may grant in a TPO any, some or all of the reliefs mentioned in the Act and shall be effective for thirty (30) days. The court shall schedule a hearing on the issuance of a PPO prior to or on the date of the expiration of the TPO. The court shall order the immediate personal seruice of the TPO on the respondent by the couft sheriff who may obtain the assistance of law enforcement agents for the service. The TPO shall include notice of the date of the hearing on the merits of the issuance of a PPO; 2.2. Violence Against Women (VAW) - refers to any act of gender-based violence that results in, or is likely to result in physical, sexual, or psychological harm or suffering to women, including threats of such acts, coercion, or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life. It shall be understood to encompass, but not limited to, the following: Physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence occurring in the family, including battering, sexual abuse of female children in the household, dowryrelated violence, marital rape, and other traditional practices harmful to women, non-spousal violence and violence related to exploitation; Physical, sexual and psychological violence occurring within the general community, including rape, sexual abuse, sexual harassment, and intimidation at work, in educational institutions and elsewhere, trafficking in women, and prostitution; and physical, sexual, and psychological violence perpetrated or condoned by the State, wherever it occurs. It also includes acts of violence against women as defined in Republic Act Nos. 9208 and 9262. Under the Magna Cafta of Women, this term is used interchangeably with gender-based violence; 2.3. VAW Desk - a facility that would address VAW cases in a genderresponsive manner, managed by a person designated by the punong barangay. It is situated within the premises of the barangay hall. In the absence of a barangay hall, the VAW Desk shall be established within the premises where the punong barangay holds office; The definition of terms provided in Republic Act No. 9710, otherwise known as the Magna Carta of Women, as far as applicable, are hereby made part of this Ordinance. a I Ord. title: Ordinance No. 0310-17

text: SCOPE AND COVERAGE. - This Ordinance shall be enforced within all barangays of the City of Davao;
title: Ordinance No. 0310-17

text: ESTABLISHMENT OF VAW DESK IN EVERY BARANGAY. 4.1. Setting up the VAW Desk - the punong barangay shall designate an area within the barangay hall for VAW desk. She/He shall provide for the necessary furniture and fixtures such as, but not limited to, table, chairs, separate filing cabinet and log books for record-keeping of cases. Likewise, the punong barangay shall ensure the confidentiality of the case and privacy and safety of the victim-survivor. 4.2. Designation of vAW Desk person the punong barangay shall designate a VAW desk person who is trained in gender-sensitive handling of cases; preferably a woman barangay kagawad or a woman barangay tanod. In cases where there are no trained personnel, ensure that the person assigned shall undergo basic gender-sensitivity training and orientation on anti-VAW laws;
title: Ordinance No. 0310-17

text: FUNCTIONS OF THE BARANGAY VAW DESK. Given the many functions of the Barangay VAW Desk (BVD), the VAW Desk Officer must report for duty from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. to respond to complaints and assist clients. The VAW Desk Officer must be accessible through landline and mobile phones and should be on call in case an accident occurs after working hours. The VAW Desk shall perform the following tasks: 5.1. Respond to gender-based violence cases brought to the barangay; 5.2. Keep VAW case records confidential and secured, and ensure that only authorized personnel can access it; 5.3. Assist victims of VAW in securing Barangay Protection Order (BPO) and in accessing necessary seruices; 5.4. Develop the barangay's gender-responsive plan in addressing gender-based violence, including support services, capacity building and referral system; 5.5. Coordinate with and refer cases to government agencies, nongovernment organizations (NGOs), institutions, and other seruice providers as necessary; 5.5. Address other forms of abuse committed against women, especially senior citizens, women with disabilities, and other marginalized groups; 5.7. Lead advocacies on the elimination of VAW in the community; and 5.8. Perform other related functions as may be assigned;
title: Ordinance No. 0310-17

text: PROTOCOL IN HANDLING VAW CASES AT THE BARANGAY LEVEL. The following protocols shall be observed by the Barangay VAW Desk person when responding to VAW situations: 6.1. Make the woman (and child/children, if applicable) comfortable in a safe and private room, giving her water and other immediate needs, if any; 6.1.2. Assess the situation and get initial information to determine the risks on hand and if immediate medical attention is needed. If so, facilitate referral to the nearest medical facility; Ord. No. 0310-17 6.1.3. After the victim-survivor has stabilized, assist the punong barangay/kagawad in the conduct of an investigation in a gender-sensitive and nonjudgmental manner in a language understood by her; 6.1.4. Inform her of her rights, the remedies available and the processes involved particularly in relation to the Barangay protection order (BpO). Assist her to file an application, if she so decides to obtain a BpO; 6.1.5. Record the incident using the Barangay Intake SheeU 6.1.6. If the victim-survivor desires to be in a safe shelter, seek the assistance of other barangay officials, barangay tanod or the police in getting her belongings and refer her to a shelter/women's center or to the City Social Seruices and Development Office (CSSDO); 6,1.7. Assist the victim-surivor to file for a Temporary protection order (TPo) or Permanent Protection order (PPo) with the nearest Famiry Court within twenty-four Qfl hours after issuance of Bpo, if the victimsurvivor so desires, or she applies directly for a TPo/PPo instead of a BPO; 6.1.8. Repoft the incident within four (4) hours to the Philippine National Police (PNP) and the city social Seruices and Development office (cssDo); 6.2. text: POWERS AND FUNCTIONS - The Maritime Coordinating Council shall have the following powers and functions: 1. Implements measures to address all maritime safety and security issues, conduct search and rescue operations, and enforce laws on environmental protection in the maritime waters within the territorial jurisdiction of Davao City in support of the concerned government agencies; Ord. No. 0362-L7 2. Sustains and monitors the protection of the maritime environment and other issues and events that may affect the local safety and security situation of Davao City in suppoft with the concerned government agencies and NGOs; 3. Maintains a constant and up-to-date City risk assessment on criminality, tenorism, maritime emergencies and smuggling happening in the maritime waters and coastal areas within Davao City and to take law enforcement actions relative thereto; 4. Develops plan to integrate and orchestrate law enforcement operations affecting public safety and security along Davao City coastal water; 5. Formulates and conducts trainings, seminars, workshops and other activities within and among concerned agencies for the proper implementation of the duties imposed in this Ordinance; 6. Facilitates the exchange of intelligence information among involved government agencies in order to reinforce and strengthen maritime law enforcement operations; 7. Analyzes and identifies target personalities, and determines the emerging threats and crimes that happened at the maritime waters of the City for possible law enforcement operations; 8. Recommends policies, plans, programs and projects for efficient interoperability operations among agencies involved in enforcing the duties imposed in this Ordinance; 9. Peforms other duties and functions as may be directed.

text: PARAMOUNT WARRI9R - Also called "Bawwangin" by the local tribes), Datu Bago was of Kagan, Tausug and Maguindanawon ancestry who setUed in Bagobo land (now known as Davao). He fought long and hard in keeping Davao Gulf free from foreign control as the whole area around the Gulf of Davao was under his control. In 1839, Datu Bago joined by the Bagobo and Kagan Tribes, struck his greatest blow against foreign invaders. Davao was the last unoccupied territory in the Philippines and Datu Bago heroically defended it against the Spaniards.

text: DEC1ARATION OF POUCY- The provisions of this Ordinance, in consonance with the City Governmenfs commitment for good governance and maintaining public order and safety, hereby declares this policy to strengthen the implementation of security measures imposed by the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP), the Philippine National Police (PNP), Rehabilitation Centers and other Law Enforcement Agencies. For this purpose, the City of Davao adheres to the following measures: a) To prevent the occurrence of deaths, riots, hostage taking and escape of inmates or patients by prohibiting the possession and entry of deadly and bladed weapons; b) To prevent the inmates or patients from coercing, intimidating, threatening complainants and witnesses or other forms of retaliation, orchestrate crimes and organize rescue plan by prohibiting the possession and entry of cellular phones and other electronic gadgets; c) To prevent the inmates or patients from bribing jail or detention center personnel or custodians by prohibiting the possession of excessive amount of money in cash or check inside jails or detention centers; d) To safeguard public health and well-being of the inmates or patients by penalizing the possession and entry of illegal drugs, alcoholic substances, cigarettes and tobaccos; and e) To promote public welfare in the community by ensuring the rehabilitation and development of inmates or patients in preparation for their eventual reintegration into the society upon release.

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS - As used in this Ordinance the following terms shall mean: 1. Assembly-Assembly occupancies include, but are not limited to, all buildings or portions of building used for gathering together nfty (50) or more persons for such purposes as deliberation, worship, enteftainment, eating, drinking, amusement, awaiting transpoftation, or similar uses; 2. Building Administrator- Any person who acts as agent of the owner and manages the use of a building for the latter; 3. Directional Markings-signs that give directional information within a building/structure or establishment. Directional markings are identified by an arrow, multiple chevrons, or a line with chevrons at one end to show the direction of exits; 4. Final Exit Door-any door leading directly to the exterior or a street level lobby; 5. Means of Egress- continuous and unobstructed route of exit from one point in a building, structure or facility to a public way; 6. Photo-luminescent Materia!-emits light that continues for a length of time after excitation by visible or invisible light after the light source has been removed; 7. Safety Signs-illuminated signs which contain information or instruction regarding safety on a signboard;

text: LOCATION OF MARKINGS- All establishments covered by this Ordinance shall ensure that photo-luminescent safety markings are placed on: 1. Doors and doorframes: a. Doodrames of final exit doors or doors leading to means of egress; b. Door handles, knobs, latches, panic devices or opening devices of final exit doors or doors leading to means of egress; 2. Stairways, handrails, ramps and steps a. Landings, mid-landings, passageways or corridors within the stairway; b. Floor number and stainryay name; c. All handrails and handrails extensions; d. Leading edge of each step and the perimeter of ramps; 3. Means of Egress a. The Floors of means of egress shall be illuminated at all points by directional markings including angles and intersections of corridors and passageways; b. All safety signs leading to means of egress and final exit doors; i. principal routes providing access to exit in open floor areas and in seruice rooms; ii. underground walkways, basements; iii. floor areas or parts thereof where the public may congregate; 4. Obstacles-all obstructions along the means of egress, stairwells, ramps, no-exit doors, etc. 5. Safety Equipment- Fire-fighting and emergency equipment such as fire extinguishers, fire hose, first aid kit, etc.

text: DECLARATION OF PRINCIPLE AND POUCY -The Local Government of Davao City hereby declares the following as its policies: 1. The Local Government shall protect and advance the right of all Dabawenyos to a balanced and healthful ecorogy in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature; 2. The Local Government shall promote permeabre paving system, in pursuing sustainable urban development, as a crucial component to the aspirations of a livable city for the Dabawenyos and thus must be established and maintained through a participative, empowered, and environmentally conscious community; 3. The Local Government recognizes the impoftant role of permeable pavement system in the recharge of the city's groundwater and aquifers; 4. The Local Government recognizes the use of permeable pavement system as a climate change mitigation and adaptation scheme as it suspends dust pafticles and retain sequestered carbon dioxide; and 5. The Local Government recognizes the need for a legislation to ensure the permeability of the City grounds to address large volumes of water runoff in urban area as part of the Revised comprehensive Development Plan of Davao City.

text: DEFINITION EI'enUS-ns used in this Ordinance, the following terms shall mean: 1. Infiltration - the process by which water on the ground surface enters the soil; 2. Pavement - the durable surface material laid down on an area intended to sustain vehicular or foot traffic, such as a road or walkway; 3. Permeability - the property of a material or solid that determines how easily fluid flows through a material; 4. Permeable Pavement system (pps) is a storm water management facility that allows water to move through void spaces within the pavement and eventually infiltrate into underlying soils; 5. Peruious - materials that allow storm water to percolate through the surface, draining it to its gaps or void spaces rather that allowing water to pass inside the material; Ord. No. 0628-18 6, Run-off - also known as overrand flow of water that occurs when excess storm water, meltwater, or other sources flows over the earth,s surface.

text: TYPES OF PERMEABLE PAVEMENT SYSTEM (PPS) - For purposes of this Ordinance, all establishments proposed for construction or those who opt to conveft their conventional pavement shall include in their design the permeable pavement system which shall be classified, but not limited, to the following types: (1) TYPE 1. PERMEABLE CONCRETE (PC) Permeable concrete shall contain mixture of conventional porfland cement, washed gravel, and water. The water to cementitious material ratio must be 0.35 - 0.45 to 1. This mixture contains little or no sand and forms a system of highly permeable, interconnected voids, (2) TypE 2. PERMEABLE GRID PAVERS (pcp) Permeable grid pavers shall contain open-cells. Cells will be fllled with gravel, sand, or a growing compound that can be planted or allows grass and other vegetation growth. This type is usually made from regular or porous concrete, clay and even plastic reinforcement; (3) TYPE 3. PERVTOUS PAVERS (PP) Peruious and porous pavers shall consist of a wide array of materials such as turfs, rocks, tiles, woods or recycled tires as long as the design has void spaces and gaps in between as runoff drainage; (4) TYPE 4. STNGLE-STZED AGGREGATE (SS) Single-sized aggregates shall be constructed by filling loose gravel, crushed stones, recycled materials, pebbles etc. directly aftei base compaction. This will not contain binding materials; (s) TypE s. coNcRETE PAVEMENT CUTOUTS (CpC) Regular concrete composition shall have cuts or patches as permeable spaces to be filled by either grass vegetation or single-sized aggregates.

text: DECLARATION OF POLICY - The City Government of Davao hereby declares the following as its policies: 1. The Local Government shall protect and advance the right of all Dabawenyos to a balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature; 2. The Local Government shall promote conservation of our forest lands in pursuing sustainable urban development, as a crucial component to the aspirations of a livable city not only for the Dabawenyos but also for the generations to come; 3. Enhancement and protection of forest lands must be established and maintained through a pafticipative, empowered and environmentally conscious community; 4. The Local Government recognizes the important role of the community in the protection and conservation of natural resources, as well as in promoting and instilling the awareness on forest conservation and protection; 5. The Local Government recognizes the need to a balance economic growth with the protection of forest lands for the attainment of sustainable growth; and 6. The Local Government recognizes the need for a legislation to ensure the protection of our forest lands by adopting the Forest Land Use Plan as part of the Land Use plan of oavao city.

text: DECLARATION OF POUCY - It is the policy of the City Government of Davao to manage efficiently the urban landscape where mobility potentials are maximized, greening programs actualized through innovative space provision, and disaster-resilience intensified through building height restrictions. The City shall continue to devise zoning and Iand use mechanisms responsive to the challenges and opportunities as may be presented by urban growth and development. The scheme for Additional floor-space credits to qualified private individuals or corporations which have allocated open spaces for the public through the Privately Owned Public Open Spaces (POPOS) program and the premium required from developers opting for additional floor areas over and above the regular height limit being imposed by the city are strategies for environment investments. The premium floor space that may be permitted in a zone for a specified fee shall provide the City an avenue for revenue generation that may be devoted to road improvement and greening programs. It shall be further declared to be the policy of the City to strictly enforce measures in accordance with existing and relevant land use provisions.

text: - For the purpose of the Rules and Regulations, the following terms and phrases shall mean as follows: 1) Obstacle Limitation Surface (OLS) - is an imaginary surface above ground that sets the height limit for building structures to ensure flight navigational safety; 2) Floor Area Ratio (FAR) is the ratio of the total plot area to the total building area and is determined by the size of the plot and the width of the road in front of the plot; 3) "Comprehensive Land Use Plan (CLUP)" shall refer to the document embodying specific proposal for guiding, regulating growth and/or development; 4) HLURB - Housing and Land Use Regulatory Board; 5) Conforming Use - a use, which is in accordance with the zone classification as provided for in the Ordinance; 6) Green Architecture - building and structure design philosophy that aims at minimal use of non-renewable and/or polluting materials and resources/energy in construction and use of a facility when completed; 7) Green Space- community space consisting of land (as parks) rather than buildings; B) Privately-Owned Public Open Spaces (POPOS) are physical spaces which are privately owned but legally required to be open to the public under a land-use law and arrangement with the City Govemment of Davao such as but not limited to plazas, terraces, atriums, small parks, view decks, playground, food park, and alleyways that connects two structures without passing through a regular street. 9) Zoning Map a duly authenticated map delineating the different zone classifications into which the whole city is divided. 10) Mean Sea Level - the zero reference point from which the Iimits shal! be measured from.

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS 1. Indigenous Cultural Community (ICC)- Refer to a group or homogenous societies identified by self-ascription and ascription by others, who have continuously lived as organized community on communally bounded and defined territory, and who have, under claims of ownership since time immemorial, occupied, possessed and utilized such territories, sharing common bonds of language, customs, traditions and other distinctive cultural traits, or who have, through resistance to political, social and cultural inroads of colonization, non-indigenous religions and cultures, became historically differentiated from the majority of Filipinos. (Rules and Regulations Implementing Republic Act No. 837t, otherwise known as the Indigenous Peoples'Rights Act of 1997) 2. Council of Elders-This is a duly constituted group of indigenous elders recognized by the state whose functions constitutes preseruation of the customs and tradition of the tribe, and provides insights and solutions to address conflict resolution and peace-building processes, spiritual practices, rituals and ceremonials. They lead the community in decision-making processes aimed at protecting and promoting the sustainable development of their ancestral domains. The Council of Elders of each tribe or each ICC has their own tradition for adjudication. 3. Customary Laws-Refer to a body of written and/or unwritten rules, usages, customs and practices traditionally and continually recognized, accepted and obserued by respective ICCs/IPs. Ord. text: Declaration of Policv. The Sexually Transmitted Infection, Human Immunodeficiency Virus and Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (STI, HIV and AIDS) are public health concerns that have wide ranging social, political and economic repercussions. As such, responding to the STI, HIV and AIDS epidemic is imbued with public interest, and thus the City Government of Davao commits itself to the fight against the epidemic. The City Government of Davao commits to make actions to (1.) prevent the spread of HIV and other STIs and mitigate any related social, psychological, and economic consequences to fight against the epidemic; (2.) To prevent the spread of the virus and mitigate any related social, psychological, and economic consequences, as follows: 1. The City Government of Davao shall establish policies and programs to prevent the spread of STI, HIV and AIDS and deliver treatment, care and support seruices to persons living with HIV in accordance with evidence-based strategies and approaches that follow the principles of human rights, gender equality, and meaningful pafticipation of communities affected by the epidemic; 2. The City Government of Davao shall adopt a multi-sectoral and culturally-sensitive approach in responding to the STI, HIV and AIDS epidemic by ensuring that local communities, civil society groups and persons living with HIV and their families, are part of the response to the epidemic; 3. The City Government of Davao shall remove all barriers to STI, HIV and AlDS-related services and shall eliminate the climate of stigma that surrounds the epidemic and the people directly and indirectly affected by it; and 4. The City Government of Davao shall consciously adhere to generally-accepted principles of human rights and adopt gender perspectives in dealing with STI, HIV and AIDS as it shall even promote value formation and employ scientifically-proven approaches. The information and education campaigns shall be carried out in all schools, training centers, workplaces and communities. Therefore it affirms that: 1. Ord. No. 0682-19 F. "Street Island" - a raised or marked-off area in the middle of the street or road designed as a guide for traffic, used as a safety island, or for separating lanes.

text: DEFINffiON OF TERMS - As used in this Ordinance, the following terms shall mean: 1. Children-at-risk (CAR) - refer to children who are vulnerable to and at risk of behaving in a way that can harm themselves or others, or vulnerable and at risk of living, pushed, and exploited to come into conflict with the law because of personal, family, and social circumstances, such as, but not limited to, the following: a. Being abused by any person through sexual, physical, psychological, mental, economic or any other means and the parents or guardians refuse, unwilling or unable to provide protection for the child; b. Being exploited sexually or economically; c. Being abandoned or neglected after diligent search and inquiry where the parents or guardian cannot be found; d. Coming from a dysfunctional or broken family or being without a parent or guardian; e. Being an out of school youth; f . Being street children; g. Being a member of a gang; h. Living in a community with a high level of criminality or drug abuse; i. Living in a situation where armed-conflict is prevalent; j. Committing victimless crimes. 2. Child - referc to a person under eighteen (18) years old and those above 18 but unable to protect themselves and/or physically or mentally incapable of doing so; 3. Interuention - refers to a SERIES of activities which are designed to address issues that cause a child to come into conflict with the law or tend to make the vulnerability in committing offienses. It may take the form of an individualized treatnent program which may include counseling, skills training, education and other activities that will enhance the psychological, emotional and psycho-social well-being of a child; 4. Parent Education - the various forms and alternative means of providing parents with information, skills and suppoft systems to assist them in their needs as their children's primary caregivers and educators. These include public and private parent education programs linked to center homes and media-based children education programs; 5. Transformative Approach are programs and interuentions that create oppoftunities fur CAR to transform as an individual, create enabling community conducive for children, develop community paftnership and volunteerism, enhance responsible parenting and embrace community oriented programs; Ord. No. 0729-t9 6. Children at Risk Transformative Community-Based Center (CARTC) - is the anchor of all community-based and psychosocial care and support program for CAR which will operate 2al7; it will serve as their transformative and transitional home.

It was only in 1848 when the Spanish conquest started to gain a ground following the arrival of Don Jose Cruz de Oyanguren, a native of Vergara, Guipuzcoa in Spain, along with his 70 comrades. The Oyanguren-led group partnered with Datu Daupan, chief of Samal Mandayas, who wanted to get even with Datu Bago. Amid Datu Bago's strong resistance, the foreign group launched massive attacks. Oyanguren ordered the establishment of palisade in Piapi for his defense and installation of causeway across swamps to bring canons within range of Datu Bago's settlement. Navy Commanding General Don Manuel Quesada also joined in the fight against Datu Bago. Their attacks prospered as Datu Bago and his defenders were outgunned, which eventually resulted to Oyanguren's possession of Davao Gulf in 1849. Oyanguren managed to possess the territory despite the lack of support from the government in Manila and his principals. Small progress was made to spur the economy of the gulf region. Oyanguren also urged the different tribes like Mandayas and Manobos to live in settlements to reach them for trade and commerce. The Moros, however, threatened those who would collaborate with the Spaniards. As way to indicate Spanish rule, Oyanguren named the Gulf Region "Nueva Vergara." lt was eventually renamed to "Davao" following the strong clamor of Davaoefios. Davao was derived from three subgroups of Bagobo indigenous peoples as the Tagabawa called the settlement "Dabo," the Guiangan dubbed it "Dawaw" and the Obo tagged it "Davah." The pioneer Christian inhabitants of the area were the proponents behind the official adoption of Davao in 1868. The native inhabitants also became Christians when Jesuit missionaries achieved to pursue conversion of religious faith in 1868. The Jesuit fathers were able to encourage the tribes to live in settlements where they can learn Christian precepts and practices. 1 Excerpts from a manuscript "Davao: An lntroduction to its History" by Ernesto l. Corcino. 2 Moros here is used interchangeably with Muslims, which refers to believers of lslam. Muslim is the preferred usage in lslamic countries in the Middle East, where lslam believers were called Moors before. Moros refer specifically to believers of lslam in Southeastern Philippines as distinguished from the Moors of earlier century, who were lslam believers in Southern Spain and North Africa. 1. The early inhabitants played a vital role to keep Davao Gulf free from foreign dominion. With the stalwart leadership of Davao Gulf Chief Datu Bago, the territory remained unscathed. Some Muslims were urged to become Christians upon the mandate of their leaders, Datu Timan and Datu Porkan, while there were still Muslims who remained steadfast in their lslam faith. Father Saturnino Urios, who labored among the Moros of Hijo in 7892, further swayed the latter's faith that led to the great divide. Those who wanted to live among the Christians left Hijo. They were resettled in Tigatto and Ma-a, under the supervision of Don Francisco Bangoy and Don Teodoro Palma Gil Sr., respectively. The separatist groups refer themselves now as Kagans. The Spaniards' reign in Davao was cut short after 50 years of occupation with the continuous resistance of the Lumads and Moros. They decided to fully abandon Davao in 1899. ln December 1898, the Americans started to colonize Davao. The American settlers, mostly retired soldiers and investors from Zamboanga, Cebu, Manila and United States, recognized the rich potential of Davao for agricultural venture as there were vast areas of primeval forest lands. Noting its rich soil, the Americans started to propagate rubber, abaca and coconut in addition to different varieties of tropical plants imported from Ceylon, lndia, Hawaii, Java and Malaysia. The robust foreign agriculture investments pulled Davao up to serves as one of the major producers of export products such as abaca, copra and lumber in the first two decades of 20th century. Davao also became a regular port of call by inter-island shipping and began direct trade linkages abroad to markets like United states, japan and Australia. ln 1903, Japanese began to arrive as they experienced spike in taxes after Meiji restoration

title: AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING THE CITY COLLEGE OF DAVAO (CCD), DEFTNTNG rTS MANDATE AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF I

text: LOCATION -The City Government of Davao will acquire a permanent site to which school buildings and other facilities will be constructed.
title: AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING THE CITY COLLEGE OF DAVAO (CCD), DEFTNTNG rTS MANDATE AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF I

text: PURPOSE- The primary purpose of the College is to help promote the interest and welfare of the people of Davao by providing them access and equitable opportunities with relevant and responsive academic and technology-driven programs for all deprived, disadvantaged and underserued learners who will be equipped with knowledge, skills, and values to compete and contribute meaningfully to the growth and development of the City and to the world at a very minimal cost. sEcrIoN 4. THE coRPoRATE PowERs oF THE COLLEGE The city College shall constitute a body corporate which shall be endowed with the attributes and perpetual succession of a corporation and shall possess the powers which peftains to a local College to be exercised in conformity with the provisions of this Charter. Fufthermore, the College shall possess the following corporate powers: 1. To have a continuous succession in its corporate name; 2. To have and use a corporate seal; 3. To exercise such powers as granted by the SANGGUNIANG panlungsod of Davao, subject to the limitations provided in this Ordinance and other laws. ARTICLE II - BOARD OF TRUSTEES
title: AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING THE CITY COLLEGE OF DAVAO (CCD), DEFTNTNG rTS MANDATE AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF I

text: BOARD OF TRUSTEES - The governing body and corporate powers of the City College shall be vested in and exercised by the Board of Trustees (BOT) composed of the following: 1. The City Mayor shall automatically be the Chairperson of the BOT. He/She shall be the Presiding Officer at every meeting of the BOT; 2. The College President shall be the Vice Chairperson of the BOT. He shall act as the Presiding Officer of the BOT in the absence of the Chairperson; 3. The Commission on Higher Education (CHED) Regional Director of Region XI, as member; 4. The Chairperson of the Committee on Education, Science and Technology, Afts and Culture of the SANGGUNIANG Panlungsod as member; 5. The President of the Faculty Association as member; 6. The President of the Supreme Student Government as member; 7. The President of the Alumni Association as member; B. The representative of the Association of Local Colleges and Universities (ALCU) as member; 9. The Chairperson of the Davao City Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Inc., as member; 10. A Representative from the Education sector as member; 11. The Indigenous People's Mandatory Representative (IPMR) of the SANGGUNIANG Panlungsod, as member. Ord. No. 0198-20
title: AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING THE CITY COLLEGE OF DAVAO (CCD), DEFTNTNG rTS MANDATE AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF I

text: The Board of Trustees shall have a Board Secretary who shall be appointed by the Chairperson and whose term of Office shall be co-terminous with the Chairperson. He shall likewise serue as the Executive Committee Secretary.
title: AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING THE CITY COLLEGE OF DAVAO (CCD), DEFTNTNG rTS MANDATE AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF I

text: The Members of the Board of Trustees shall have the following term of office: 1. The Chairperson - during his/her term as City Mayor; 2. The Vice-Chairperson for a term of four (4) years, subject to reappointment; 3. The Chairperson, Committee on Education, Science and Technology, Arts and Culture, SANGGUNIANG Panlungsod - during his/her term as a Member of the Sanggunian; 4. The Schools Division Superintendent (SDS) - during his/her term as SDS of the Division of Davao City; 5. The Faculty Representative - one (1) year; 6. The Student Council Representative - one (1) year; 7. The Indigenous People's Mandatory Representative (IPMR) of the SANGGUNIANG Panlungsod - during his/her term as IPMR. The Chairperson of the Committee on Education, Science and Technology, Arts and Culture of the SANGGUNIANG Panlungsod; 3. The Faculty Representative of the CCD; 4. text: COMPOSITION OF TTIE MENTAL WELLNESS CENTER - The Facility shall have two (2) components - the halfiruay home for recovered, abandoned, homeless and neglected persons with mental disability (the halfuiay home), and the community-based mental wellness center (the wellness center), respectively. The proper names of both these components shall be determined as fit at a later time. The halfrvay home is a post-recovery home that provides shelter to recovered persons with mental disabilities who are abandoned, neglected and homeless and found living or staying on the streets. Its staff composition and operating procedures shall be in consonance with the provisions of the Mental Health Code of Davao City, as well as the accepted standards in the practice. The City Health Office shall take the lead in the management and superuision of the Shelter, while the City Social Services and Development Office (CSSDO) shall provide for after-care seryices at the community level when the persons are reintegrated back to their respective families and communities. Ord. No. 0210-20 The Mental Wellness Center shall function as a community-based facility which will provide immediate access to various psychiatric and psychological seruices. The CSSDO and the City Health Office shall take the lead in the management and operations of the Mental Wellness Center.

text: ADMISSION TO THE FACILITY - Due to the distinct nature of the Shelter ftom the Counseling Center, there shall be a different set of criteria for admission to each. text: DEFINITION OF TERMS - The following terms used in this Ordinance shall mean: 1. Frontline Workers or Frontliners - are defined as persons employed in, whether regular, casual, contractual, project based, job order, part-time, or other forms of employment, or exercising essential frontline functions, such as: a. Health workers, such as doctors, nurses, hospital or clinic aids, administrative staff, laboratory technicians, pharmacists and drug store employees; b. Employees of the national, local and barangay units tasked to work on the fronUines; c. Members of the AFP, PNP, PCG, BFP, and other law enforcement agencies; d. Employees of non-government organizations assisting in health, safety, disaster or emergency response such the Philippine Red Cross, World Health OrganizaUon, and the like; e. Employees of banks, bayad centers, money transfer services, cooperative and savings establishments, and the like; f . Employees of groceries, convenience stores, wet markets and the like; g. Employees of food preparation, manufacturing and delivery services; h. Those operating publk utility vehicles such as taxis, jeepneys, and trirycles; i. Those working in essential private service sectors such as security guards, janitors, caretakers, funeral parlors, drivers of cargo vehicles and vehicles hired to transport other frontline workers, business process outsourcing or call centers, LPG and gas stations, water refilling stations, and the like; and j. Mass media personnel. 2. Patients - are deflned as: a. Confirmed Case - any individual, irrespective of the preserrce or absence of clinical signs and symptoms, who was laboratory confirmed for COVID-19 in a test conducted at a DOH certified laboratory testing facility. b. Suspected Case - are those identified by DOH guidelines as falling under such classification; c. Probable Case- are those identified by DOH guidelines as falling under such classiflcation. Provided, that any change in classification of the DOH of cases shall fall under the cabeEory of "patients" under this Ordinance. Ord. No. 0255-20 3. Close Contact - is a person without proper personal protective equipment who is providing direct care for a confirmed COVID-19 case, or a person which has direct physical contact, or lived, worked, transacted or travelled in close proximity (less than 1 rneter) for more than 15 minutes with a confirmed COVID 19 case, provided that any change by DOH of this definition shall be adopted automatically under this Ordinance. SE TION 3. PROHIBITED ACTS A. No person, natural or juridical shall be allowed to: 1. Discriminate against, or hiring, engaging, influencing others to discriminate against frontliners, patients or close conbacts or analogous circumstances: a. Dishonoring existing contractual obligations such as lease contracts, including the refusal to allow entry into such leased premises, solely by reason of being a frontliner, patient or a close contact; b. Performing any form of coercion or harassment to force or influence a person to leave a leased or shared premises, solely by reason of being a frontliner, patient or close contact; c. Removing or firing a person from employment, solely by reason of being a frontliner, patient or close contacfi d. Refusal to follow set guidelines by the appropriate government agencies on hazard pay, special risk allowance, or other mandatory benefits, allowances or compensation; e. Refusal of entry into or expelling frontliners from groceries, convenience stores, markets, palengkes, banks, bayad centers or other financial services, and the like; f. Refusing to allow frontliners access to basic services such as food preparation and delivery, transportation, laundry, healthcare, medicine, and the like, 2. Commit any act intended to prejudice against, cause injury to, or harass or those which shall tend to cause shame or humiliation to frontliners, patients, or close contacts, or hiring, engaging, influencing others to do the same, Such as: a. Any form of physical, mental or emotional violence or abuse; b. Any form of coercion or threat of physical, mental or emotional violence; c. Any form of financial or economic abuse such as, but not limited to, refusing loans or forfeiting those already granted, rejecting valid payments, failing to properly compensate, denying any support legally due, solely by reason of being a frontliner, patient or close contact; Ord. No. 0255-20 d. Disclosing the information of a person, including, but not limited to, his/her name, known address, place of work or employment, known alias, medical details, or implying the identity of, or claiming that a person - whether verifled or not by DOH - is a frontliner, patient or close contact, unless done so with the permission of such individual or DOH; e. Any form of cyber-bullying or the sharing of classified or private communication without the consent of all involved in the same, or any malicious acts done online, whether the information shared be true or made-up, against the name, dignity or honor of a frontliner, patient or close contact; 3. Any other act of discrimination or prejudice against which demeans, reduces or nullifies the enjoyment or exercise of a frontliner, patient, or close contact's human and legal rights, or hiring, engaging, influencing others to do the same. B. In addition to the above acts, it shall be unlawful for any public official, employee, health or medical seruice provider or law enforcement officer to refuse assistance, deny seruice to or block aid, or hiring, engaging, influencing others to do the same, to a frontliner, patient or close contact who wished to enforce his/her rights, unless such person is in violation of the guidelines of the Department of Health and other existing laws.

text: BUILDING PERMIT PROCESSING TIME _ The different offices involved in the OSSCP, functioning as one unit, shall evaluate simple Building Permit applications with complete documentary requirements, within a maximum period of five (5) working days. The Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) shall process the Fire Safety Evaluation Clearance (FSEC) within a maximum period of three (3) working days and shall abide by the manual operations that will be developed in relation to Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2018-01 dated January 4,20L8 issued by the Depaftment of the Interior and Local Government (DILG), the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH), the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICD and the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) and other supplemental manuals that shall be separately prepared by individual OSSCP. For easy compliance by the applicant, applications with deficiencies shall be issued a Comprehensive Correction Sheet and/or a Notice of Disapproval by the Zoning Officer, City Building Official (OBO), and the local Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) stating all deflciencies. For applications that satisfy the requirements of the Zoning Ordinance, the OSSCP shall release the Building Permit, together with the locational clearance, other ancillary permits and the Fire Safety Evaluation Clearance (FSEC,) after payment of appropriate fees and charges. The Office of the City Building Official (OBO) shall provide the local BFP and the City Assessor's Office with the list of the issued Building Permits on a monthly basis (every 5th day of the month) for their reference, in anticipation of the applicant's future application for a Ceftiflcate of Occupancy.

text: ASSESSMENT OF FEES - After the evaluation of the building permit application, the Zoning Officer, the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP), and the Office of the Building Official (OBO) shall simultaneously prepare an Order of Payment that will be issued to the applicant, at the same time, specifying the fees that the applicant is obligated to pay in accordance with the provisions of the Zoning Ordinance, the National Building Code of the Philippines (NBCP), the Fire Code of the Philippines (FCP) and the City's Revenue Code. The Zoning Officer, the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) and the Office of the City Building Official (OBO) shall put in place the necessary measures to implement a one-time assessment of building-related fees and charges which shall include the local fees for securing the locational clearance, barangay clearance, filing fees among others. The fees for the issuance of the Fire Safety Evaluation Clearance (FSEC) under the Fire Code of the Philippines shall be based on the estimated value of the building or structure declared by the owner or applicant duly notarized. In the event that there is substantial difference between the estimated value of the building or structure as declared by the owner or applicant from the amount indicated in the application for the building permit, the higher value will be adopted. The Office of the Building Official (OBO) and the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) may collect a fling fee, in addition to the NBCP and FCP prescribed fees and charges, to cover costs incurred in assessing building permit and FSEC applications. text: Definition of Terms - For purposes of this Ordinance, the following terms are hereby defined as follows: a. Mag-Negosyo Ta Day (MTD) Program - is a program targeted specifically for women to engage or already engaged in the production, processing or manufacturing of products or commodities, including agro-processing, trading and seruices, whose total assets including those arising from loans but exclusive of the land on which the particular business entity's office, plant and equipment are considered micro business, either with physical store or selling through online platform, situated in Davao City. It aims to alleviate poverty and promote and guarantee the civil and socio-economic rights of women residing in Davao City; b. Woman/Women - those who are biologically female, aged 21 years and above, of sound mind, and who are capable of establishing and managing business enterprises; For purposes of this Ordinance, these shall include women members of Indigenous Peoples, Moro/ Muslim, Tribal and Lumad Groups, disadvantaged and vulnerable women, marginalized women who are most victimized by poverty and injustice, mothers of child laborers, unemployed, underemployed, senior citizens, victim-survivors of violence, trafficked and prostituted women, solo parents, displaced overseas and local workers, street/ambulant vendors, online sellers, grassroots rural women, small farmers and rural workers, fisherfolk, urban poor, women with special needs, and women from left behind families; c. Assets - refers to all kinds of propefties, real or personal, owned by the accredited women members, entrepreneurs and qualified beneficiaries of the MTD Program and used for the operation and conduct of its business; d. Loan - cash, goods, machineries and equipment with an obligation to return the value of cash, goods, machineries and equipment without payment of interest; e. Grant - cash, goods, machineries and equipment without the obligation to return the value or amount but subject to liquidation and monitoring; f . Staft Up Capital - includes funds for any operational expenses to be incurred prior to the launching of the business, its products and services; g. Capital Enhancement - includes funds for any operational expenses of an already established business entity which aims to enhance the overall value of the business, its production and seruices; Ord. Depaftment of Labor and Employment (DOLE)- accredited Associations - group of women formally organized and accredited by DOLE for purposes of application for grants to which they are qualified; i. text: DEFINITION OF TERMS. a) Public Health Authority - refers to the Department of Health (DOH), IATF-EID, the City Health Office, or any person directly authorized to act in behalf of the aforementioned. b) COVID-19 - a potentially severe respiratory illness caused by a coronavirus and characterized by fever, coughing, and shortness of breath, the spread of which is the reason the World Health Organization has declared a worldwide pandemic. c) Quarantine - a state or place of isolation for a person or groups of persons who may have come in contact with contagious diseases, and is not reserved for sick peoPle onlY. d) Fourteen (14)-day home quarantine- a quarantine protocol aligned with the l4-day period of incubation of the COVID-19 virus. As per the World Health Organization (WHO), the guidelines are as follows: 1) Allocate a separate room with adequate ventilation at home if possible. Household members should stay in another room or should be separated from the returnee; 2) Maintain at least one meter distance from family members. 3) Other household members should use a separate bathroom. If sharing the same bathroom, cleaning of taps, doorknobs and utensils with soap and water are a requirement. 4) Minimize visitors in the house. The person under isolation should not interact with any visitors. 5) Frequent handwashing with soap and water for at least twenty (20) seconds at a time and maintain alcohol-based hygiene in instances where handwashing facilities are inadequate. 6) Avoid touching eyes, nose and mouth with unwashed hand' 7) The home quarantined person is expected to monitor body temperature using a thermometer twice a day. If he/she develops fever, cough, difficulty in breathing, sore throat, body aches and pain, including flu-like symptoms, immediately inform local health authorities. Ord. No. 0325-20 B) After use, disposable facemasks should be properly discarded. 9) Assign separate dishes, drinking glasses, cups, eating utensils, towels, beddings and other items for the quarantined person. 10)Used utensils, bed linen and clothes should be washed with soap and water. e) Rapid Antibody Test - also know as Rapid Test (RT), is an Antibody Test that qualitatively detects the presence of IgM and IgG antibodies against the COVID-19 virus in human serum, plasma and venous whole blood specimen for the auxiliary diagnosis of covlD-19 infection. Reverse Transcription Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR)- a COVID-19 test using actual swabs from patients taken from the nose or throat. This test determines the actual presence of the coronavirus and if a person is currently infected. g) Asymptomatic - when a disease exists in a person without noticeable symptoms. h) permanent Resident Visa- a document granted to foreigners, granting them the right to reside in the Philippines on a permanent basis. i) Locally Stranded Individuals (LSI) - Foreign nationals or Filipino citizens in a specific locality within the Philippines who have expressed intention to return to their place of residence/home origin. LSIs may be further classified AS: 1) Workers; 2) Students; 3) Tourists; and 4) Other individuals stranded in various localities while in transit i) Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs) - overseas Filipinos whose primary reason for being outside the country or for leaving the country is due to a contract of employment in a foreign nation or a vessel flying another nation's flag. k) Non-Overseas Filipino Workers (Non-OFWs) - overseas Filipinos whose primary reason for being abroad is not due to a contract of employment in a foreign nation or vessel. l) Returning Overseas Filipinos (ROFs)- Filipino citizens who are returning to the Philippines from abroad. They are categorized into: 1) OFWs, whether documented or non-documented 2) Non-Overseas Filipino Workers (non-OFWs): i. Returning students ii. J1 visa holders/ exchange visitor's program iii. Returning Filipino Diplomats iv. Returning FiliPino Tourists v. ParticipantsofPhilippinegovernment-sponsored programs vi. Dependents and accompanying foreign spouses Ord. No. 0325-20

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS - The Definitions and Terms used in the revised Implementing Rules and Regulations of the National Health Insurance Act of 1995 (Republic Act No. 7875) are hereby adopted. As used in this Ordinance, the following terms shall mean: 1. PHILHEALTH (PHIC) - refers to the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation created under Republic Act No. 7875, otherwise known as the National Health Insurance Act of 1995 2. PHILHEALTH CLAIMS - refers to claims filed by the seruice provider with the PHIC to recover the costs/expenses incurred in the treatment of patients. There are two (2) PHIC claims separately, the PAY TO HCI claims and the PAY TO PROFESSIONAL FEE claims 3. MARILOG DISTRICT HOSPITAL TRUST FUND ACCOUNTS - refers to the PHIC, HCI and PF accounts, account for other hospital claims and fees, and donations 4. PROFESSIONAL FEES (PF) - refers to PHIC reimbursements for professional seruices rendered by health providers in the hospitals 5. HEALTH CARE INSTITUTION (HCI) - refers to health care provider institution 6. HMO - refers to the Health Maintenance Organizations 7. INSTITUTIONAL EXPENSES -refers to the expenses that shall be incurred for trainings needed for accreditations and for any other licensing requirements, emergency purchases or the unforeseen expenses that are not included in the Manual Of Operation.

text: CREATION OF THE MARILOG DISTRICT HOSPITAL TRUST FUND - There is hereby created a Marilog District Hospital Trust Fund. This hereby create three (3) accounts, which shall be maintained to draw accounts from the proceeds of the following: Ord. No. 067L-2L PHIC claims paid to the Health Care Institution (MDH); PHIC claims that are separately issued by PHIC to Professional Fees; Claims from financial assistance, grants, subsidies, insurances, Health Maintenance Organizations (HMO), and co-payments. The City Accountant's Office and other relevant offices are hereby tasked to cause the assignment of allotment class and account code pursuant to the recent government accounting system on all sum accruing to this fund. Accounts accruing from the different PHIC claims shall be treated separately and distinctly from each other as stipulated in the PHIC disbursement of claims. All other charges, fees, and other income received from the management and operations not given to PHIC shall be remitted and deposited by the City Treasurer to the Marilog District Hospital Trust Fund. All Donations received by the Davao City Government intended for the development and operation of the Marilog District Hospital shall also be deposited by the City Treasurer to the said Account. SECTTON 5. PHILHEALTH CIRCULAR NO.OO35, SERIES OF 2013: . GENERAL RULES state that: *A. COMPUTATION OF THE PHIC REIMBURSEMENTS 1. For medical case rates, the HCI fee and PF shall be seventy percent (70o/o) and thifi percent (30%) of the case rate amount respectively. 2. For procedure case rates, the following shall be the basis for computation except for specified cases: 2.a. The PF shall be computed as RVU-Relative Value Unit x 56 x 1.5 except for specified case rates. 2.b. The HCI fee shall be the remaining balance when the PF is subtracted from the case amount. B. DISTRIBUTION OF THE PHIC REIMBURSEMENTS 1. The entire case rate amount, including the PF shall be paid directly to the HCI concerned to the HCI (MDH) ACCOUNT and to the PROFESSIONAL FEE. The HCI shall act as the withholding tax agent for the PF. 2. The PF shall be distributed by the HCI within thirty (30) calendar days from the date of receipt of reimbursement, Policies and procedures on the distribution of PF shall be drafted and enforced by the HCI based on the agreements between the HCI and the Professionals. Reports of noncompliance to this provision shall be forwarded to the Health Care Delivery Management Division (HCDMD) and shall be included as a violation of the HCI to the Health Care Provider Performance Commitment of the PHIC. 3. text: DISBURSEMENT OF THE MDH TRUST FUND _ ThC fUNd created under this ordinance shall be disbursed in the manner that will serue exclusively and strictly for the following purposes: A. Purchase of medical equipment, B. Purchase of medical supplies, C. Purchase of diagnostics and laboratory reagents and supplies, D. Purchase of office supplies, E. Purchase of vehicles, F. Construction of hospital facilities, G. Repair and maintenance of equipment and facilities, H. Institutional expenses, I. Honoraria for paid services/ specialists, J. Incentives for individuals/ institution for the referral of patients, K. Community extension seruices (corporate social responsibilities), and L. Other related expenses. The appropriation shall be based on the Annual Operation Plan and the Projected Procurement Management Plan of the hospital and on the Memorandum of Agreements between the hospital and the specialists, individuals or institutions for the seruices and referral incentives. SECTTON 7. DISBURSEMENT OF THE CLAIMS FROM FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE. INSURANCES, HEALTH MAINTENANCE ORGANIZATIONS (HMO), AND CO-PAYMENTS - The proceeds from these claims shall go to the General Fund of the City Government and shall be used for hospital needs, health programs of the City Health Office, and other health related activities. The professional fees covered under this SECTION shall not be subjected for inclusion and distribution among the hospital personnel to the pooled amount from PHIC. The Marilog District Hospital's Governing Board through its administrator, shall submit to the City Treasurer its annual work and financial plan. Provided that, all disbursements or withdrawals from the Marilog District Hospital Trust Fund shall be based on the approved annual work and financial plan passed by the Governing Board. Programs or projects not included in the work and financial plan may be funded through appropriate board resolution duly approved by the Marilog District Hospital Governing Board. title: AN ORDINANCE REGUTATING AND ALLOWING MOBITE FOOD TRUCK VENDORS TO OPERATE WITHIN THE DESIGNATED FOOD ZONES IN TltE CITY OF DAVAO, AS AMENDED \

text: DECLARATION OF POUCY. It is the policy of the State to promote the health, safety and general welfare of the citizens of Davao City by requiring that mobile food establishments provide its constituents with a consistent level of cleanliness, quality and safety. Towards this end, this Ordinance is enacted to provide reasonable guidelines and restrictions for mobile food establishments in relation to established restaurant businesses and to ensure the safe and convenient use of the public right-of-way.
title: AN ORDINANCE REGUTATING AND ALLOWING MOBITE FOOD TRUCK VENDORS TO OPERATE WITHIN THE DESIGNATED FOOD ZONES IN TltE CITY OF DAVAO, AS AMENDED \

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS. 1. Mobile Food Vendor - shall mean any vending unit, truck, trailer, temporary establishment or pushcaft that is not a permanent restaurant that serves food or drink to the public. For the purpose of licensing, mobile food vendors shall be defined as one of the following: a. Food truck Vendor shall mean a retail food establishment that repofts to and operates from a commissary and is readily moveable, a motorized wheeled vehicle or a towed wheeled vehicle designed and equipped to serue food. b, Seruice Truck Vendor shall mean a seruice establishment which is readily movable, a motorized wheeled vehicle or a towed wheeled vehicle designed and equipped to provide seruices on the go. c. Mobile Delivery Vendor shall mean a vendor who delivers and sells perishable and non-perishable goods, which is readily movable, is a motorized wheeled vehicle or a towed wheeled vehicle designed and equipped to provide the perishable or non-perishable items to go. d. Pushcaft shall mean a non-self-propelled vehicle limited to seruing commissary prepared or pre-packaged food and non-potentially hazardous food, unless the equipment is commercially designed and approved to handle food preparation and seruice. Pushcafts shall not be required to comply with mobile vehicular safety requirements. e. Temporary Food Establishment shall mean a retail food establishment, other than a licensed food truck vendor or pushcaft, that is not intended to be permanent and that operates at a fixed location in conjunction with a single event or celebration. 2. Commissary - shall mean an approved catering establishment, restaurant or other location approved by the governing body of the jurisdiction in which it is located in which food, containers or supplies are kept, handled, prepared, packaged or stored as related to a mobile food vending unit. 3. Extended/Mobile Food Permit - A food seruice permit acquired from the Business Bureau on a yearly basis that allows a mobile food vending unit to be allowed at pre-approved areas. 4. Food Zone - is an area approved by the City Government through the Mobile Food Vendor Committee (MFVC) for the specific operation of mobile food vehicles and/or pushcarts within the public right-of-way. t Ord. No. 0728-21 5. Hours of Operation - are the designated time frame mobile food vehicles are authorized to operate within the city rights-of-way. 6. Vending Site - shall mean a mobile retail food establishment location at which a mobile food vendor as permitted to offer food for sale. Vending site shall not refer to the commissary or place at which the mobile food vendor unit is approved to be stored when not in use. 7. Pedestrian - is a person who is walking or othenruise traveling in the public rights-of-way.
title: AN ORDINANCE REGUTATING AND ALLOWING MOBITE FOOD TRUCK VENDORS TO OPERATE WITHIN THE DESIGNATED FOOD ZONES IN TltE CITY OF DAVAO, AS AMENDED \

text: EXTENDED/MOBILE FOOD PERMIT - In case of mobile food vendors, this SECTION shall apply in lieu of the Business Permit requirement under SECTION 94, of the Revenue Code of 20L7. The term "extended/mobile food permit" shall be the business permit applicable for mobile food vendors. It shall be unlawful for any person or business to sell, or offer for sale, food of any type from a food truck, seruice truck vendor, mobile delivery vendor, pushcaft or temporary food establishment without first having secured a permit therefore from the City Mayor and paying the necessary fees to the City Treasurer. There shall be collected and annual fee at the rate provided hereunder for the issuance of an Extended/Mobile Food Permit to every person whether natural or juridical that shall conduct a mobile food business within the City of Davao. For purposes of the Extended/Mobile Food Permit, the following definition of business size is here adopted: CHARACTERISTICS Cottage Php 499,999.00 and below Small Php 500,000.00 up to Php 1,999,999.00 Medium Php 2,000,000.00 to Php 9,999,999.00 Large Php 10,000,000.00 and above The following shall be the graduated fixed taxes applicable for mobile food vendors: Cottage Php 2,000.00 Small Php 5,000.00 Medium Php 8,000.00 Large Php 10,000.00

The fee for the issuance of an Extended/Mobile Food Permit shall be paid to the City Treasurer upon application before any business or undeftaking can be lawfully begun or pursued and within the first twenty (20) days ofJanuary of each year in case of renewal thereof. For a newly-stafted business or activity that stafts to operate after January 20, the fee shall be reckoned from the beginning of the calendar quarter. When the business or activity is abandoned, the fee shall not be exacted for a period longer than the end of the calendar quarter.
