text: COMMITTEE ON CHILDREN PROTECTION AGAINST SEXUAL ABUSE. A Committee is hereby created to address the issue on sexual abuse against children. It shall be composed of the following: Chairperson - Special Office for Children's Concern (SOCC) Vice-Chairperson - City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO) Secretariat - Integrated Gender and Development Division (IGDD) Members: 1. Representative of Local Council for the Protection of Children (LCPC) 2. Representative of the Barangay Council for the Protection of Children (BCPC) 3. Representative from Local Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) working on Children's Rights 13. Representative from private schools The Committee shall have the following duties and functions: 1. Overall function. It shall lead in attaining the objective of this Ordinance pafticularly in building the capacity of the local community in giving protection to children against sexual abuse by harmonizing the roles and efforts of the responsible agencies herein established. 2. Implementation oversight and monitoring. It shall be responsible to oversee and monitor the implementation of this Ordinance. 3. Meetings. It shall convene regularly to discuss any matters relevant to the issue, formulate policies, objectives, guidelines and/or other matters to have an efficient and effective implementation of this Ordinance. Ord. No. 0854-22 4. Inter-agency coordination and linkages. The SOCC and CSWDO, being the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson respectively, shall ensure the proper coordination and linkages of the responsible agencies in executing their roles provided herein. 5. Data Modernization. It shall relevant information submitted to them by the responsible agencies gathered in the course of executing their roles. The data shall be used to conduct situation analysis in order to formulate supplemental measures and strategies to fufther enhance and strengthen protection of children against sexual abuse. A systematic approach shall be established. Thus, the following mechanisms may be considered. a) Establish a Profiling System from the information submitted to them by the responsible agencies. b) Establish and maintain a master list and database of children all-over the city. The SOCC shall coordinate with the barangays and concerned agencies for the regular submission of relevant child-related information. These records peftaining to the information given to them shall be confidential and shall only be disclosed to proper authorities. c) Utilize the data gathered and provide a Situation Assessment and Analysis on Children relative to protection of children against sexual abuse. It shall also determine who are the children considered at a high-risk of being sexually abused and provide recommendations and action plans thereof to the Committee. The Situation Analysis can be used to identiff who are the children considered at a high-risk of being sexually abused and determine the risk factors and conditions that contribute to the incident such as: i. Risky behaviors of the perpetrator; ii. Handicapped victims or children with disabilities; iii. Povety-stricken families; iv. Out-of-school youth; v. Dysfunctional households and abusive parents; vi. Those who live in isolated and/or far-flung remote communities' and vii. Other risk factors and conditions. d) As an end-product, provide a Local State of Children Repoft policy proposals and guidelines on how to address the situation and provide better protection for children against all forms of sexual abuse. e) The report shall be submitted to the Office of the City Mayor for any purpose it may deem proper. 6. Ensuring the functionality of programs and interuentions. It shall conduct periodic assessment regarding the programs and interuentions provided by responsible agencies. Identify the gaps existing therein and determine which programs and interuentions are non-functioning or has overlapping functions and those which are ineffective, inefflcient and needs reconsideration, and provide remedies thereto. Ord. No. 0854-22 It must ensure that these programs and interuentions are age-appropriate, gender-sensitive and culturally-appropriate. It shall always provide utmost consideration to the best interest of the child. 7. Initiating Partnership with other agencies. It shall have the initiative to tap additional workforce and advocates for children protection such as Nongovernment Organizations (NGOs), Civil Society Organizations (CSOs), Faithbased Organizations and other volunteers and invite them to have joint effofts in combating sexual abuse on children, B. text: DECLARATION OF PRINCIPLES AND POLICIES A. Sedion 3 Rule I of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 10121 Declaration of Poliq - It is the Poliq of the State to: a. Uphold the people's constitutional rights to life and property by addressing the root causes of vulnerabilities to disasters, strengthening the country's institutional capacity for disaster risk reduction and management, and building the resilience of local communities to disasters including climate change impacts; b. Adhere to and adopt the universal norms, principles, and standards of humanitarian assistance such as the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, UN Guiding Principles and Guidelines on Internal Displacement and Durable Solutions, Convention on the Elimination of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW), Convention on the Rights of the Child and the global effoft on risk reduction as concrete expression of the country's commitment to overcome human sufferings due to recuning disasters; c. Incorporate internationally accepted principles and guidelines of disaster risk management in the creaUon and implementation of national, regional and Ioca! sustainable development and poverty reduction strategies, policies, plans and budgets; d. Adopt a disaster risk reduction and management approach that is holistic, comprehensive, integrated, and proactive in lessening the socioeconomic and environmental impacts of disasters including climate change, and promote the involvement and pafticipation of all sectors and all stakeholders concerned, at all levels, especially the local community; e. Develop, promote, and implement a comprehensive National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Plan (NDRRMP) that aims to strengthen the capacity of the national government and the Local Government Units (LGUs), together with paftner stakeholders, to build the disaster resilience of communities, and - to institutionalize arrangements and measures for reducing disaster risks, including projected climate risks, and enhancing disaster preparedness and response capabilities at all levels; f. Adopt and implement a coherent, comprehensive, integrated, efficient and responsive disaster risk reduction program incorporated in the development plan at various levels of government adhering to the principles of good \i Ord. No. 0866-22 governance such as transparency and accountability within the context of povefi alleviation and environmental protection; g. Mainstream disaster risk reduction and climate change adaptation and mitigation in development processes such as policy fonnulation, socioeconomic development planning, budgeting, and governance, particularly in the areas of environment, agriculture, water, energy, health, education, poverty reduction, land-use and urban planning, budgeting, and governance, pafticularly in the areas of environment, planning, public infrastructure, and housing, among others; h. Institutionalize the policies, structures, coordination mechanisms and programs with continuing budget appropriation on disaster risk reduction from national down to local levels towards building a disaster-resilient nation and communities; i. Mainstream disaster risk reduction into the peace process and conflict resolution approaches in order to minimize loss of lives and damage to propefi, and ensure that communities in conflict zones including Internally Displaced Percons (IDPs) can immediately go back to their normal lives during periods of intermittent conflicts; j. Ensure that disaster risk reduction and climate change measures are gender responsive, sensitive to indigenous knowledge systems and cultures, and respectful of human rights; k. Recognize the local risk patterns across the country and strengthen the capacity of LGUs for disaster risk reduction and management through decentralized powers, responsibilities, and resources at the regional and local levels; l. Recognize and strengthen the capacities of LGUs and communities in mitigating and preparing for, responding to, and recovering from the impact of disasters; m. Engage the participation of Civil Society Organizations (CSOs), the private sector and volunteers in the governmenfs disaster risk reduction programs towards complementation of resources and effective delivery of services to the citizenry; n. Develop and strengthen the capacities of vulnerable and marginalized groups to mitigate, prepare for, respond to, and recover from the effects of disasters; o. Enhance and implement a program where humanitarian aid workers, communities, health professionals, government aid agencies, donors, and the media are educated and trained on how they can actively support breastfeeding before and during a disaster and/or an emergenry; and Ord. Provide maximum care, assistance and seruices to individuals and families affected by disaster, implement emergency rehabilitation projects to lessen the impact of disaster, and facilitate resumption of normal social and economic activiUes. B. SECTION 12 (a) of Republic Act No. 10121states that "there shal! be established a Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office ([DRRMO) in every province, city and municipality, and a BDRRMC in very barangay which shall be responsible for setting the direction, development, implementation and coordination of disaster risk management programs within their territorial jurisdiction"; C. Accreditation, Mobilization, and Protection of DisasterVolunteerc and National Service Reserue Corps, CSOs and the Private Sector. - The government agencies, CSOs, private sector and LGUs may mobilize individuals or organized volunteers to augment their respective personnel complement and logistical requirements in the delivery of disaster risk reduction programs and activities. text: DECLARATION OF PRINCIPLES AND POLICIES A. The City Government of Davao is committed to the maintenance of peace and security within its jurisdiction, as a safe and peaceful environment is vital to the progress of a city when there are no risks and threats to its development. B. Implementing and policymaking bodies are created for the purpose of peacebuilding. C. Therc are eight (8) broad categories that create and sustain peaceful societies. The Institute for Economics and Peace has identified the following eight (8) Pillars of PosiUve Peace as the most common characteristics of most peaceful societies. These pillars are: . Well-functioning government; o Low levels of corruption; . Acceptance of the rights of others; . Good relations with neighbors; . Sound business environment; o High level of human capital; . Equitable distribution of resources; and o Free flow of information. The concept of Positive Peace acknowledges that ending direct violence alone does not guarantee durable peace. Ending direct violence is Negative Peace. For peace to endure, a society must build longer-term conditions that enable society to unify and flourish. This is called Positive Peace. Investing in Positive Peace improves resilience, mitigates risks of violence, and reduces the economic toll from conflict. The Eight-Pillars of Positive Peace are highly interconnected and interact together to build a system. It therefore requires building capacities for peace, not only of the government, but also of local communities and other structures and institutions of the city. The establishment of Peace 911- The Center For Peacebuilding will contribute to the achievement of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals of the United Nations, in particular, Goal 16 on building peace, justice and strong institutions, strengthening human rights, reducing discrimination and inequality, promoting gender equality, preseruing natural resources and protecting the climate. text: DECLARATION OF POLICY - Along some streets of Davao City are untidily scattered with idle poles, strewn with abandoned and unused wires, cables and unbundled or nonfunctional overhead electrical wires and communication cables that not only present unpleasant sight and view but also posing hazard to persons and propefties. This Ordinance aims to regulate the maintenance of abandoned wires, cables and poles considered as nuisance within the City. This will create a safe and clean environment for individuals protecting them from harm or injury that may be caused by abandoned wires, cables and poles. Ord. No. 0B9B-22
title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING THE MAINTENANCE OF IDLE POLES AND ABANDONED WIRES AND CABLES IN THE CITY OF DAVAO

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS - For purposes of this Ordinance, the following terms are defined: 3.1 Abandoned wires - refer to wires and cables installed and seruing no purpose; 3.2 Barangay Inventory-refers to the inventory submitted by the barangay consisting of a list of all abandoned wires, cables and idle poles within their jurisdiction, with actual pictures of the color-coded wires, pole number and exact location; 3.3 Cable- an assembly of one or more insulated conductors or optical fibers within an enveloping sheath that supply electricity or telecommunications signals; 3,4 Color-coded wires - refer to wires and cables marked with ceftain colors that identify the ownership of such wires; 3.5 Idle poles - refer to all poles installed which are no longer in use or dilapidated; 3.6 Incident Report - refers to the report issued by the Wires and Cables Technical Team after a priority-tagging of the Barangay inventory; 3.7 Nuisance - refers to any act, omission, establishment, business, condition of property, or anything else which injures or endangers the health or safety of others; 3.8 Overhead Lines - all kinds of wires and cables installed overhead; 3.9 Pole - refers to utility poles or columns used to support attachments for all kinds of overhead lines, cables and accessories.
title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING THE MAINTENANCE OF IDLE POLES AND ABANDONED WIRES AND CABLES IN THE CITY OF DAVAO

text: GUIDELINES AND REGULATED ACTS - The following acts shall be obserued in the implementation of this Ordinance: 4,1 Removal of Abandoned Wires and Idle Poles - Abandoned wires and idle poles that are considered as nuisance must be removed within thity (30) days from receipt of a written notice. Any wire or cable that is not removed on the 3'd offense shall be removed by the Ancillary Seruices Unit subject to the permission of the Wires and Cables Technical Team. 4.2 Bundling of Wires and Cables - Loose, unbundled or cluttered wires, and cables that are still in seruice shall be bundled or bound together to form a single unit by the use of zip tie, tie wire or by lashing, or by the use of any other strong and safe material. An Incident Repoft must be filed with the Wires and Cables Technical Team. Violations under this Ordinance must be treated per Incident Repoft. Failure to obserue the abovementioned acts shall be a violation of this Ordinance and shall be penalized accordingly. For this purpose, the barangay shall be informed prior to any installation of wires and cables within their jurisdiction.

NCDA shall lead in the implementation of programs and projects for the disabled.

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS (a) Ambulant, Transient or Itinerant Vendor - refers to a vendor or seller who does not permanently occupy a definite place of the market but one who comes either daily or occasionally to sell his/her goods. (c) Basic Deposit Account (BDA) - refers to interest or non-interest bearing bank account with an initial minimum deposit of no more than One Hundred Pesos (PhP100.00), no minimum maintaining balance, no dormancy charges, maximum balance of Fifty Thousand Pesos (PhP50,000.00) and with simplified know-your<ustomer or KYC requirements. The list of e-money issuers (EMI) or entities authorized by BSP to offer e-money account can be found on the BSP website: https://bit.lylBSPSupervisedEMls. (i) Financial Seruice Providerc (FSP) - means a regulated financial institution which is licensed and superuised by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas. QR Codes store information using patterns of black dots and white spaces, ananged in a square grid. It can be read by a smaftphone r:rmera that is equipped with a bar-code reader. text: DECLARATION OF POLICIES - Davao City recognizes the vital role of the youth in nation-building enshrined in the 1987 Philippine Constitution. It shall promote and protect their physical, moral, spiritual, intellectual and social well-being. Thus, it shall be the policy of Davao City to defend the rights of the children and provide special protection from all forms of sexual abuse that are prejudicial to their development. Specifically, the City shall provide comprehensive measures and strategies in combating the proliferation of sexual abuse against children by engaging and harmonizing the efforts of governmental and non-governmental agencies. The City shall continue its tireless effort in giving priority to the rights of the children especially in terms of protection which led the City in consistently winning awards as one of the best child-friendly cities in the country, among others.
title: AN ORDINANCE PROVIDING FOR PREVENTION AND INTERVENTION MECHANISMS IN PROTECTING CHILDREN AGAINST ALL FORMS OF SEXUAL ABUSE AND EXPLOITATION

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS. 1. Center-based programs - refer to the programs in an establishment where people can seek to avail strategic programs, seruices and interuentions developed for purposes of protecting children against sexual abuse. 2. Child (Children) - for purposes of this Ordinance, child (children) refers to person(s) below eighteen (18) years of age or those over but unable to fully take care of themselves and protect themselves from sexual abuse because of physical and/or mental disability condition. (CWC 2019, with minor edits) 3. Child (Children) at high-risk against rape - refers to a child who is exposed to a higher level of danger against sexual abuse compared to other children due to risk factors and conditions affecting him or her. 4. Child Pornography - the unlawful or prohibited acts defined and punishable by Republic Act No. 9775 or the Anti-Child Pornography Act of 2009, committed through a computer system: Provided, That the penalty to be imposed shall be one (1) degree higher than that provided for in Republic Act No. 9775. 5. Community-based programs - refer to the programs provided by persons, offices or organizations through approaching the communi$l with strategic programs, seruices and interuentions developed for purposes of protecting children against sexual abuse. 6. Consciousness building - an approach to a child in awakening and/or improving his or her state of mindspecifically in realizing the evil sought by sexual abuse and his or her vulnerability to it. 7. Cybersex against a child - the willful engagement, maintenance, control, or operation directly or indirectly, of any lascivious exhibition of sexual organs or sexual activity, with the aid of a computer system, for favor or consideration against a child. t Ord. No. 0854-22 B. Empowerment - an approach to a child in making him or her stronger and more confident specifically in protecting his or her right against sexual abuse. 9. Responsible agencies -these are the agencies that are mentioned and given specific roles in this Ordinance. 10. Sexual abuse on child - refers to an act in which a child is abused for sexual gratification. It includes direct sexual contact, engagement in indecent exposure (of the genitals, nipples, etc.), pornography, prostitution and other forms of sexual gratification involving a child.

text: COMMITTEE ON CHILDREN PROTECTION AGAINST SEXUAL ABUSE. A Committee is hereby created to address the issue on sexual abuse against children. It shall be composed of the following: Chairperson - Special Office for Children's Concern (SOCC) Vice-Chairperson - City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO) Secretariat - Integrated Gender and Development Division (IGDD) Members: 1. Representative of Local Council for the Protection of Children (LCPC) 2. Representative of the Barangay Council for the Protection of Children (BCPC) 3. Representative from the Sanggunian Kabataan (SK) Federation 4. Representative from Davao City Police Office (DCPO) 5. Representative from City Information Office (CIO) 6. Representative from City Health Office (CHO) 7. Representative from the Division Office of the Depaftment of Education (DepEd), through its Division Office B. Representative from the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCrP) RO Xr 9. Representative from the National Commission of Muslim Filipinos (NCMF) RO XI 10. Representative from the Commission on Human Rights (CHR) RO XI ll.Representative from Local Media Board 12. Representative from Local Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) working on Children's Rights 13. Representative from private schools The Committee shall have the following duties and functions: 1. Overall function. It shall lead in attaining the objective of this Ordinance pafticularly in building the capacity of the local community in giving protection to children against sexual abuse by harmonizing the roles and effofts of the responsible agencies herein established. 2. Implementation oversight and monitoring. It shall be responsible to oversee and monitor the implementation of this Ordinance. 3. Meetings. It shall convene regularly to discuss any matters relevant to the issue, formulate policies, objectives, guidelines and/or other matters to have an efficient and effective implementation of this Ordinance. Ord. No. 0854-22 4. Inter-agency coordination and linkages. The SOCC and CSWDO, being the Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson respectively, shall ensure the proper coordination and linkages of the responsible agencies in executing their roles provided herein. 5. Data Modernization. It shall relevant information submitted to them by the responsible agencies gathered in the course of executing their roles. The data shall be used to conduct situation analysis in order to formulate supplemental measures and strategies to further enhance and strengthen protection of children against sexual abuse. A systematic approach shall be established. Thus, the following mechanisms may be considered. a) Establish a Profiling System from the information submitted to them by the responsible agencies. b) Establish and maintain a master list and database of children all-over the city. The SOCC shall coordinate with the barangays and concerned agencies for the regular submission of relevant child-related information. These records pertaining to the information given to them shall be confidential and shall only be disclosed to proper authorities. c) Utilize the data gathered and provide a Situation Assessment and Analysis on Children relative to protection of children against sexual abuse. It shall also determine who are the children considered at a high-risk of being sexually abused and provide recommendations and action plans thereof to the Committee. The Situation Analysis can be used to identiff who are the children considered at a high-risk of being sexually abused and determine the risk factors and conditions that contribute to the incident such as: i. Risky behaviors of the perpetrator; ii. Handicapped victims or children with disabilities; iii. Povefi-stricken families; iv. Out-of-school youth; v. Dysfunctional households and abusive parents; vi. Those who live in isolated and/or far-flung remote communities; and vii. Other risk factors and conditions. d) As an end-product, provide a Local State of Children Report policy proposals and guidelines on how to address the situation and provide better protection for children against all forms of sexual abuse. e) The repoft shall be submitted to the Offlce of the City Mayor for any purpose it may deem proper. 6. Ensuring the functionality of programs and interuentions. It shall conduct periodic assessment regarding the programs and interuentions provided by responsible agencies. Identify the gaps existing therein and determine which programs and interuentions are non-functioning or has overlapping functions and those which are ineffective, inefficient and needs reconsideration, and provide remedies thereto. Ord. No. 0854-22, It must ensure that these programs and interuentions are age-appropriate, gender-sensitive and culturally-appropriate. It shall always provide utmost consideration to the best interest of the child. 7. Initiating Partnership with other agencies. ,It shall have the initiative to tap additional workforce and advocates for children protection such as Nongovernment Organizations (NGOs), Civil Society Organizations (CSOs), Faithbased Organizations and other volunteers and invite them to have joint effofts in combating sexual abuse on children. text: DECLARATION OF POLICIES AND PRINCIPLES - It has been the policy of the Local Government of Davao City to ensure the viability and growth of Cooperatives and People's Organizations as instrument of social justice, equity, self-reliance, economic development and people empowerment. Republic Act No. 9L78 or the Barangay Micro Business Enterprises (BMBES) Act of 2002 recognizes the role of BMBEs as essential driving force for the country's economic development. The BMBEs are seedbeds of Filipino entrepreneurial talents and strengthening them would increase job generation, provide livelihood and better quality of life. Republic Act No. L0744, otherwise known as the Credit Surety Fund Cooperative Act of 2015, aims to increase the credit worthiness of MSME which otherwise cannot obtain loans from banks due to lack of acceptable collateral, credit knowledge and credit track records. Said program complements the LGU's povefi alleviation programs by creating more economic activities and job oppoftunities, thus contributing to the revenues of the city. The Bayanihan to Recover as One Act 2 of 2020 (R.A. LL494) directs all National Government agencies (NGAs) such as the Depaftment of Trade and Industry (Dn), Department of Science and Technology (DOST), Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA), Department of Agriculture (DA), Depaftment of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) and Depaftment of Agrarian Reform (DAR) in consonance with their given mandate, are implementing Socio-economic Recovery Program such as Livelihood and Skills Training Program for their respective targeted beneficiaries pafticularly the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, especially those affected by the COVID-l9 pandemic. The City's thrust on poveilry alleviation towards socio-economic development under its Socio-economic cluster spearheaded by the City Cooperative Development Office (CCDO) and depaftments such as the City Agriculturists's Office (CAO), City Veterinarian's Office (CVO) and the City Social Welfare Development Office (CSWDO) and other line offices through the Livelihood'Assistance Program (LAP), have been providing financial assistance and livelihood projects and grants since 1999 through the passage of Administrative Order No. 2, SERIES of 1999; Executive Order No. 17, SERIES of 2005; and Executive Order No. 08, SERIES of 2009. Under existing Executive Order No. 01, SERIES of 2015, an Order prescribing the Guidelines, Rules and Procedures Enhancing the Livelihood Assistance Program to be known as Enhanced Livelihood and Enterprise Assistance Program (ELEAP) of Davao City has to conform in accordance with Republic Act No. 11032, othenruise known as the "Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Seruice Delivery Act of 2018" which seeks to increase the efficiency of the delivery of government seruices, establish effective practices and prevent graft and corruption in the government. Thus, ensuring timely and efficient delivery of seruices in the releases of financing assistance packages to targeted beneficiaries. tt Ord, No. 0855-22 Therefore, the Ordinance institutionalizing the Davao City Sustainable Livelihood and Entrepreneurship Program (DCSLEP) is the City Government's vital and essential legislation for socio-economic reversals in line with the City's program thrust (Byaheng DO30) on povety alleviation. Such can only be achieved by funding through equity infusion for the program and strengthen coordination and linkages with identified stakeholders in the government and private sector.

No. 0855-22 0 MSME GRANTS - is a financial assistance program coming from national and international fund sources allocated to the Local Government Unit to fund specific livelihood projects. The purpose of this program is to strengthen the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMES) in Davao City through the provision of equipment/material support and capabi lity-building activity. g) Al! other similar Livelihood Assistance Program from the National Government Agencies and other Non-Government Organizations that would support the City's thrust on poverty alleviation towards socio-economic development.

text: - The City of Davao shall ensure that its culture and tradition is appreciated, promoted and preserved. To take this into fruition, the City shall ensure that its local culture shall showcase the beautiful culture and rich tradition of its eleven (11) Uibes, by requiring city government employees to wear an Indigenous People or Moro inspired attire and/or accessories, every first Monday of the month. SECTIOI{ 3. SIEE - This Ordinance shall be limited to government employees of this City, regardless whether such employee holds Office or employment in casual, contractual, temporary, holdover, permanent or regular capacity. This shal! also apply to newly-hired employees, Job-Order and Contract of Seruice employees. Moreover, those whose ethnicity is outside the domain of the eleven (11) tribes of Davao City may wear their respective ethnic attire. Finally, a genuine or authentic Indigenous People or Moro inspired attire, may be worn by the abovementioned government employees, provided that, a ceftification from the Office of the Cultural Community Affairs has been secured from the said Office, agency or department, as required under SECTION 6 of Ordinance No. A307-L7, SERIES of 20t7, otherwise known as the "IP Attire Ordinance".

text: rc. - Whenever used in this Ordinance, the following terms shall mean as herein set forth: a) Ceftification - shall refer to any document evidencing that a prior consultation for the use of an Indigenous Peoples Attire has been secured by an office, agency or departnent from the Office of the Cultural Affairs. b) City Government Employees - shall refer to those employed by the Davao City Government. c) Indigenous Peoples Inspired Attire - shall refer to inspired garments, clothes or accessories which generally represent the five (5) tribes of the Indigenous People of Davao City, to wit, hgobo, Klata, Ata, Obo Manuvu, Matigsalug and Bagobo-Tagabawa tribes. d) Inspired Attire - shall refer to garments, clothes or accessories which is inspired by existing elements of the eleven (11) tribes of Davao City as prescribed under this Ordinance; e) Moro Inspired Attire - shall refer to inspired garments, clothes or accessories which generally represent the six (6) Moro tribes of Davao City, to wit: Tausug, Sama, Maranao, Maguindanaon, Iranun and Kagan tribes. 0 Office or employment in casual or contractual capacity - shall refer to those whose employment in the government is in accordance with a special contract to undeftake a specific work or job, requiring special or technical skills not available in the employing agency, to be accomplished within a specific period, which in no case shall exceed one (1) year and performs or accomplishes the specific work or job, under his own responsibility with a minimum of direction and supervision from the hiring agency. No. 086-22 g) Office or employment in Holdover capacity - shall refer to an employee who is entitled to hold his office until his successor shall have been duly chosen and shall have qualified. h) Office or employment in permanent or regular capacity - shall refer to a permanent appointment which is extended to a person possessing the requisite qualifications, including the eligibility required, for the position, and thus protected by the constitutional guaranty of security of tenure. i) Office or employment in Temporary Gapacity - shall refer to the issuance to an employee who meets all the requirements for the position to which he is being appointed except the appropriate civil service eligibility and shall not exceed 12 months. j) Tribal Accessories - shall exclusively refer to the accessories of the eleven (11) tribes of Davao City.

text: MANDATORY WEARING OF IP AND MORO INSPIRED ATTIRE - It shall be required for all City government employees in the City of Davao to wear an Indigenous Peoples Inspired Attire or Moro Inspired Attire and/or accessories based on the eleven (11) tribes of Davao City, every first Monday of the month to celebrate the local culture. City government employees who belong to any of the eleven (11) tribes in Davao City can likewise wear their authentic attire. City government employees whose ethnicity is outside the domain of the eleven (11) tribes of Davao City, may likewise wear their respective ethnic attire. This shall be required for all city government employees, whether holding casual, contractual, hold-over, permanent and/or temporary capacity.
title: Ordinance No. 086-22

text: EXCEPTIONS - The following acts or employees shall be exempted from the implementation of this Ordinance: 7.1 Those who are regularly peforming their duties and functions in the field, and those assigned in actual field operations; 7.2 When the nature of the work of the concerned employee demands that he or she wears a clothing other than what is imposed in this Ordinance; 7.3 Those who are prohibited to wear such attire by reason of their religious affiliation; 7.4 Those employees who have lost a loved one may wear their mourning clothes during their period of mourning; and 7.5 Pregnant female employees who need to wear their maternity clothes. Page,4 of 5 Ord. No.086-22 SECTIOil 8. M - An Indigenous People or Moro inspired attire is appropriate when it does not diminish the value of the cultural heritage of the Indigenous People of the Moro tribes of the City. A prescribed pattern shall be incorporated to the inspired attire as approved by the eleven tribes, to be worn by the City govemment employees, such as but not limited to, their uniforms or office-issued shifts. The eleven (11) tribes shall likewise prescribe the accessories that may be worn by the City government employees, in lieu of the inspired attire. This prescribed pattern and/or accessory are those commonly known to be used or are representation of each of the eleven tribes in Davao City, as approved by their Council leaders to be correct and appropriate in accordance with their tradition and practice.
title: Ordinance No. 086-22

text: DECLARATION OF PRINCIPLES AND POLICIES A. The City Government of Davao is committed to building and maintaining a peaceful society where its citizens have the capacity to lead long, happy lives which is ultimately the goal of all development. Peacebuilding should therefore be a cross-cutting theme in any development plan or program. Peacebuilding is the process of increasing connectors and decreasing dividers so that equitable development can occur. On the other hand, development is the process of increasing capacities and decreasing vulnerabilities so that people's choices are expanded to enable them to lead long happy lives. B. There are eight broad categories that create and sustain peaceful societies. The Institute for Economics and Peace has identified the following eight (B) Pillars of Positive Peace as the most common characteristics of most peaceful societies. These pillars are: . well-functioning government; . low levels of corruption; o dcc€ptance of the rights of others; o good relations with neighbors; o SoUr.ld business environment; . high levels of human capital; . equitable distribution of resources; and . free flow of information. The concept of Positive Peace acknowledges that ending direct violence alone does not guarantee durable peace. Ending direct violence is Negative Peace. For peace to endure, a society must build longer-term conditions that enable society to unify and flourish. This is called Positive Peace. Investing in Positive Peace improves resilience, mitigates risk of violence, and reduces the economic toll from conflict. The Eight Pillars of Positive Peace are highly interconnected and interact together to build a system. It therefore requires building capacities for peace not only of the government but also of local communities and other structures and institutions of the City. The establishment of Peace 911-The Center for Peacebuilding will contribute to the achievement of the t7 Sustainable Development Goals of the United Nations, in pafticular Goal 16 on building peace, justice and strong institutions, strengthening human rights, reducing discrimination and inequality, promoting gender equality, preseruing natural resources and protecting the climate. text: DECLARATION OF POLICY - It shall be the policy of the Local Government of Davao to seek organized means and systematic methods of institutionalizing the Alternative Learning System (ALS). Towards this end, the City shall provide out-of-school children in special cases and adults with oppoftunities to improve their knowledge, values, life skills, and readiness for higher education, work or self-employment through a system of non-formal or indigenous education, or both which are tailored to respond to their learning needs and life circumstances. The City shall also ensure the close paftnership and collaboration with the barangays and private sectors.

text: OBJECTMS This Ordinance aims to achieve the following objectives: a. Provide adequate, timely and quality attention and suppoft to the basic learning needs of out-of-school children in special cases and adults including indigenous people; b, Guarantee equitable access for all learners, including those who reside in the unreached, underserued, conflict-affected communities and communities in emergency situations to avail of systematic, flexible and appropriate alternative basic education program outside of the formal school system; d. Hire, capacitate, and deploy ALS Teachers, Community ALS Implementors and Learning Facilitators to deliver a range of ALS programs especially in far-flung, unserued, underserued, conflict-affected communities, and communities in emergency situations; e. Design specialized programs for learners with disabilities, taking into consideration their different levels of learning needs and other functional difficulties in the development of instructional materials and learning resources in accessible format; t. Develop, integrate, and utilize non-formal and informal education approaches and strategies in the delivery of the ALS programs and the assessment of learning outcomes and competencies of ALS learners by providing flexibility in the duration of learning programs, learning contents, and delivery strategies, among others; g. Improve access education and other learning oppoftunities and raise the level of literacy to contribute to an individual's sustainable future; and c. Promote lifelong learning oppoftunities anchored on the Alternative Learning System (ALS), K to 12 Basic Education Curriculum (BEC) that takes a holistic, integrated and inter-sectoral approach, and provide pathways across modes of learning which will ensure that learners will become caring, self-reliant, independent, productive and patriotic citizens, by allowing such learners to pursue further education, after pafticipating in the ALS program and passing the accreditation and equivalency assessments or ceftifications, or both required by the Depaftment of Education (DepEd), or seek employment; i i i Ord. No. 0893-22 h. text: DEFINITION OF TERMS - For purposes of this Ordinance, the following shall mean: a. Alternative Learning System Teacher (ALS Teacher) - shall refer to DepEd employed teachers who implement the ALS program. c. Adult - shall refer to a person at least eighteen (18) years of age and above. d. Alternative Learning Sytem (ALS) - shall refer to a parallel learning system that provides a viable alternative to the existing formal education instruction. It encompasses both non-formal and informal source of knowledge and skills. e. Basic Literacy Program - shall refer to the program component of ALS that is aimed at eradicating illiteracy among out-of-school children in special cases and adults by developing basic literacy skills of reading, writing, numeracy, and simple comprehension. f. Community Alternative Learning System Implementors (Community ALS Implementors) - shall refer to persons engaged either by the Depaftment of Education or any Local Government Unit (LGU) to deliver ALS programs to out-of-school children in special cases and adults. g. Community Learning Center (CLC) - shall refer to a physical space to house learning resources and facilities of a learning program for out-ofschool children in special cases and adults. It is a venue for a face-to-face learning activities and other learning oppoftunities for community development and improvement of the people's quality of life. h. Indigenous Peoples (IP) - refer to a group of people of homogenous societies identified by self-ascription and ascription by others, who have continuously lived as organized community on communally bounded and defined territory, and who have under claims of ownership since time immemorial, occupied, possessed and utilized such territories, sharing common bonds of language, customs, tradition and other distinctive culture traits or who have, through resistance to political, social and cultural inroads of colonization became historically differentiated from the majority of the Filipinos. Ord. No. 0893-22 i. Indigenous Peoples Education - shall refer to the program that supports education initiatives undeftaken through formal, non-formal, and informal modalities with emphasis on any of, but not limited to, the key areas of indigenous knowledge systems and practices and community history, indigenous language, Indigenous Learning System (ILS), and community life cycle-based curriculum and assessment, educational goals, aspirations and competencies specific to the Indigenous Cultural Community (ICC), engagement of elders and other community members in the teachinglearning process, assessment, and management of the initiative, recognitional and continuing practice of the community's ILS, and the rights and responsibilities of ICCs. j. Informal Education - shall refer to diverse forms of learning that are international or deliberate but are not institutionalized. It is a lifelong process of learning by which every person acquires and accumulates knowledge, skills, attitudes and insights from daily experiences at home, at work, at play and from life itself towards literacy. k. Learners with Disabilities - shall refer to those who have long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments which in interaction with various barriers may hinder their full and effective participation in society on equal basis with others. l, Learning Facilitators - shall refer to teachers financed by the private sector who implement ALS programs. The private sector shall include nongovernment organizations or associations, civic society organizations, or individuals. m. Micro-Ceftification, also known as micro-credentialing - shall refer to a flexible means of certifying attainment of specific elements of ALS K to 12 minimum competencies which can be used by the holder as credential such as in job application, recruitment and selection. n. Non-Formal Education (NFE) shall refer to any organized and systematic educational activity carried outside the framework of the formal education system to provide selected types of learning to a segment of the population. o. text: DECLARATION OF POLICY - It is hereby declared that Davao City recognizes tourism as an indispensable component of the Clty's socio-economic development. It is likewise acknowledged that, to establish Davao City as the prime hub and center for conventions and congresses, the City shall adopt policies and enact legislative measures for efficient and effective operations of the MICE Industry. This Ordinance intends to: a) provide measures that will position Davao City as a top desired destination for regional, national, and international Meetings, Incentives, Conventions, and Exhibitions (MICE); b) enact policies that will strengthen the Meetings, Incentives, Conventions, and Exhibitions (MICE) industry in the City; and c) set the direction of the Meetings, Incentives, Conventions, and Exhibitions (MICE) industry; SECTIOI{ 3. DEFII{ITION OF TERMS. - Whenever used in this Ordinance, th€ following terms shall mean as herein set forth: a) MICE shall refer to the Meetings, Incentives, Conventions, and Exhibitions events industry. b) MICE events shall refer to MlCE-related activities including social and business meetings, congresses, conventions, incentive trips, product presentations, business courses, conferences, and seminars. c) Meetings shall mean any number of people coming together in one pafticular place for a particular activity, which can be a one-time event or recur regularly. d) Incentives are typically given to employees as rewards. A non-business vacation with the aim of continued motivation for performance. Incentives may include incentive travel or trip. e) Conventions are events that have specific objectives and exchanges of information. 0 Exhibitions are those where displayed products or services are the event's primary focus.

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS - For purposes of this Ordinance, the following terms are defined: 2.1 Percons with Disability (PWDs) are defined by Republic Act No.7277 or the Magna Cafta fior Disabled Persons as persons suffering from restriction of different abilities, as a result of a mental, physical or sensory impairment, to peform an activity in the manner or within the range considered normal for a human being. An impairment is any loss, diminution or aberration of psychological, physiological, or anatomical structure of function. Disability shall mean (1) physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more psychologica!, physiological or anatomical function of an individual or activities of such individual; (2) a record of such an impairment; or (3) being regarded as having such an impairment. Persons designated by law as PWDs, such as Cancer Survivors pursuant to Republic Act No. 11215 or the National Integrated Cancer Control Act, persons with Rare Diseases under Republic Act No. LA747 or the Rare Diseases Act of the Philippines, and other related laws shall be considered as PWDs. 2.2 A Cinema or Movie theater is a venue, usually a building or located within malls, that contains seating for an audience for the purpose of public enteftainment. It is a commercial operation that plays films or movies fur paying customers. 2.3 PWD ldentification Card (PWD ID)refers to the official Identification Cards issued by the City Govemment of Davao to persons classified as PWDs. It shall bear the name, picture and type of disability of the PWD; 2.4 Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) refers to a company's voluntary - commitment to conduct business in an ethical way, and to contribute to the development of society and the local communrty. SECTIOil 3. GUIDELINES AND REGULATIOilS - The following acts shall be obserued in the implementation of this Ordinance: 3.1 FREE MOVIE PRMIEGE. Persons with Disability with duly issued PWD IDs shall enjoy the privilege of free movie access to any film of their choice, in a cinema or movie theater. The free movie privilege shall be non-transferable and may only be availed of by the PWD. If the PWD cannot personally transact with cinema personnel, he/she may be represented by his/her companion for transaction purposes, provided, they are present during the transaction. Cinemas or cinema operators Ord. No.0155-23 must strictly implement a 'NO PWD ID, NO ENTRY" policy. The PWD must also present his/her movie pass booklet upon entry. The free movie privilege only applies to regular movie screenings, excluding specialcinemas such as Dolby Atmos, IM$(Theaters, Dirccb/s Club, and 3D and 4D theaters. For blockbuster films, the ftee movie privilege may only be availed of during its second week. The said privilege does not extend to screenings for special events such as sponsored movie premierc, pay-per-view shows, and the like. 3.2 MOVIE PASS BOOKLET. The Persons with Disabilities Affairs ffice (PDAO) shall issue availing PWDs with a Movie Pass Booklet. The said booklet shall contain the serial number, PWDs full name, photo, address, PWD ID number, and signature. The booklet shall also contain the dates and number of movies that the PWD may avail of during the entire year. The movie pass booklet shall be non-transferable and must be presented by the PWD to the cinema personnel upon entry. 3.3 VERIFICATIOII. For purposes of verification of PWD IDs, Cinema Operators must refer to the Philippine Registry for Person with Disability Website (PRPWD). Should cinema operators wish to conduct fufther verificaUon, they may also contact the Records SECTION of the City Social Welfare and Development ffice (CSWDO) at (082) 286-3689. 3.4 AVAILMEilT. The free movie pass may be availed of only by Pl/tlDs registered under the City Government of Davao. They may avail of the free movie privilege once a week, every Monday, and during the first screening only. However, cinemas are not prohibited fiom offering the ftee movie privilege on additional days of the week. The free movie pass is good for one screening only per week. Should the PWD opt to screen another movie on the scheduled ftee movie privilege day, they will have to pay the regular movie entrance with the 20olo discount provided for under the law. 3.5 PARTICIPATING CINEMAS. The Memorandum of Agreement shall provide the specific day and time when the privilege may be availed of, the allotrnent of seats for PWDs, and the proof of identification rcquired to be presented to avail of the free movie access in the available movie theaters of the cinema operators. i.. Ord. No.0155-23 The free movie privilege granted to PV1/Ds under this Ordinance shall be counted under the cinema's Corporate Social Responsibility program. 3.7 MONITORING SHEET. Cinema owners and operators must provide a monthly monitoring sheet where the PWDs will register their full name, signature, and PWD ID number upon availing of the privilege. The Monitoring Sheet shall serue as proof of compliance to this Ordinance, and must be available at any time for tracking purposes. 3.8 PIOSTERS AND NOTICES FOR PUBTIC AWARENESS. All cinemas within the jurisdiction of the City of Davao are required to display posters or notices on the cinema booths where cinema viewers transact to buy tickets. The posters or notices shall be written in big, legible text and shall contain the privilege of PWDs to free movie access, the date and time of scrcening, and the number of seats allotted br PWDs who may avail of the said access. However, PWD viewers may opt to sit anywhere aside from the reserved seats within the cinema to their liking. text: DECLARATION OF POLICY - The Local Government of Davao City acknowledges the mandate of the 1987 Philippine Constitution pafticularly Article II, SECTION D(, which states that "The State shall adopt an integrated and comprehensive approach to health development which shall endeavor to make essenUal goods, trealth, and other social seruices available to all people at affordable cost. There shall be priority for the needs of the underprivileged, sick, elderly, disabled, women and children". Fufthermore, Republic Act No. 9994 or the "Expanded Senior Citizens Act of 20L0' provides that a Healthy and Productive Ageing Program for senior citizens shall be provided. This program prinrarily ainrs to promote quality life anrong older persons and contribute to nation building through providing equitable access to quality healthcare. In addition, relevant laws such as Republic Act No. 1L223 or the "Univercal Health Care Act", pafticularly SECTION 6 (a) states that "Every Filipino shall be granted immediate eiigibility and access to preventive, pronrotive, curative, iehabilitative and palliative care for medical, dental, mental, and emergency health services, delivered either as a populationbased or individual-based health services. Moreover, Republic Act No. 10645 or the Act for the Mandatory PhilHealth (PHIC) Coverage for all Senior Citizens states that "All senior citizens shall be covered by the national health insurance program of PhilHealth." Lastly, Depaftment of Health Administrative Order (DOH-AO) 2015-0009 or the "National Policy on the Health and Wellness Program for Senior Citizens" further solidifies the various legal mandates and direct the Local Government Units on organizing the seruice delivery networks in managing and implementing the health and wellness program for senior citizens activities, passage of necessary local legislation to inrplement the activities and provide counterpart funds for implementing their invesUnent plan that supports the healthy and productive aging of the senior citizens (a.k.a. older adults). The City also affirms the value of the Filipino tradition of caring for the older adults who also took care of us and in recognizing their contribution to the community as we look upon for their guidance in making Davao City a better place to live in. The City recognizes the valuable contribution of the older adults, and commits to the improvement of their well-being by providing a "Healthy and Productive Ageing Program", a community-based program, exclusive for clients 60 yearc old and above, who are residents of Davao City'. It shall cater basic health seruices needed by older adults and it shall be progressive and other health programs shall be integrated to meet the needs of the clientele.

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS a) Ageiiig - at the biological level, is a process resulting from the impact of the accumulation of a wide variety of molecular and cellular damage overtime, which leads to gradual decrease in physical and mental capacity, a growing risk of disease and ultimately death (WHO). -1 Ord. No. 0156-23 b) Geriatrician - is a physician who is specially trained to evaluate and manage the unique healthcare needs and treatment preferences of older people. He/ She is a Board-Certified Internist or Family Physician who has additional training and certifi cations in geriatrics. c) Healthy and Productive Ageing Program - focuses on promoting the health and wellness of older adults and alleviating the conditions of older percons who are encountering degenerative diseases. This program primarily aims to promote quality life among older persons and contribute to nation building through providing equitable access to quality healthcare and provide the necessary seruices to promote the quality of life of older persons. d) Home Visitation - A professional, purposefu! interaction that takes place in the family's residence aimed at promoting, maintaining or restoring the health of the family or its members. e) Medical Nutrition and Diet Therapy (MNDT) - a key component of holistic nutrition education and management. MNDT is defined as a "nutrition-based treatment provided by a Registered Nutritionist-Dietitian". It includes "a nutrition diagnosis as well as therapeutic and counselling services to help manage certain health conditions/disease". Fufther providing medical nutrition and diet therapy through the application of nutrition care process for the purpose of disease prevention, promotion and management that promotes nutritional health and well-being of individuals, groups, communities and population. f) Nutritionist-DietiUan or a Registered ilutritionist-Dietitian (Rt{D) - a licensed professional in the field of nutriUon and dietetics that provides medical nutrition and diet therapy to people with ceftain health conditions through the application of the Nutrition C.are Process (RA No. 10862, or the Nutrition and Dietetics Law of 2016). g) Senior Citizens or older adults or advance-aged adults - refer to the following: (a) any resident citizen of the Philippines at least sixty (60) years old; (b) must be registered to their respective Office of Senior Gtizen Affairs (OSCA), and (c) must have an OSCA ID upon availment of services.

text: IIIE - This Ordinance shall be known as "THE ANTI-BULLYING ORDINANCE OF DAVAO CITY.'
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: POUCY DECLARATION - It is hereby declared the policy of the City of Davao to ensure that the fundamental rights of persons to life, liberty, property, and security are promoted and protected. As a society composed of persons, the City recognizes the impoftance of individuality and the free exercise thereof as an essential ingredient of a well-functioning democracy. The practice of bullying, however, shall be met with disdain as it is a form of abuse which serves to deprive others of the free exercise of their own rights. In consonance with the national government's poliry under Republic Act No. 10627 declaring acts of bullying as unacceptable, Republic Act No. 11313 where both men and women must be safe and secure not only in private but also in public spaces, online, workplaces, and educational institutions, and other pertinent national laws, all forms of bullying shall not be countenanced.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: ACTS OF BULLYING -"Bullying" as adopted from Republic Act No. 10627, shall refer to any severe or repeated act by one or more persons through a written, verbal or electronic expression, or a physical act or gesture, or any combination thereof, directed at another individual that has the effect of actually causing or placing the latter in reasonable fear of physical or emotional harm to himself or damage to his propefi; creating a hostile environment at the schoo!, workplace, or any other situation for the individual; infringing on the rights of the individual; or materially and substantially disrupting the education process or the orderly operation of a school, workplace, or any other area, venue, or situation; such as, but not limited to, the following: a) Any unwanted physical contact between the bully and the complainant, such as punching, pushing, shoving, kicking, slapping, tickling, headlocks, inflicting pranks, teasing, fighting and the use of available objects as weapons; b) Any act that causes damage to an individual's psyche and/or emotional well-being; c) Any slanderous statement or accusation that causes an individual undue emotional distress, such as directing foul language or profanity at the target, name-calling, tormenting and commenting negatively on an individual's looks, clothes and body; d) Cyberbullying or any bullying done through the use of technology or any electronic means. Bullying shall be further classified into four (4) aspects, namely: a. Bullying in educational institutions b. Bullying in the workplace c. Cyberbullying d. Bullying in other public places Any person who commits the acts described above is considered a bully. Persons who, through the acts described above, retaliate against another person who repofts acts of bullying or who provides information during an investigation or is a witness under such investigation, shall also be considered to have committed bullying. Ord. No. 0L92-23
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: ACTS OF BULLYING Iil EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS - RefeT to any severe, or repeated use by one or more students of a written, verbal or electronic expression, or a physical act or gesture, or any combination thereof, directed at another student that has the effect of actually causing or placing the latter in reasonable fear of physical or emotional harm or damage to his propefi; creating a hostile environment at school for the other student; infringing on the rights of another student at school; or materially and substantially disrupting the education process or the orderly operation of a school, such as, but not limited to, the following: 1. Any unwanted physical contact between the bully and the victim like punching, pushing, shoving, kicking, slapping, tickling, headlocks, inflicting school pranks, teasing, fighting and the use of available objects as weapons; 2. Any act that causes damage to a victim's psyche and/or emotional well-being; 3. Any slanderous statement or accusation that causes the victim undue emotional distress like directing foul language or profanity at the target, name-calling, tormenting and commenting negatively on victim's looks, clothes and body. Educational institutions covered under this Ordinance include public or private schools, regardless of educational level, such as: a) Preparatory schools; b) Primary schools; c) Secondary schools; d) Colleges and universities, including post-graduate; e) Vocational schools; 0 Review centers, tutorial centers, and other similar establishments; g) Training institutions by virtue of education such as On-the-Job training as well as other activities performed off-school, but for educational purpose/s. Persons liable for bullying under this SECTION include, but are not limited to, the following: i. Students; ii. Trainees, interns, exchange students, and volunteers; iii. Teachers, student-teachers and non-teaching staff; iv. School Administrators; v. Parents and guardians of students; vi. Other authorized persons within the school campus; vii. Visitors. All acts and repofts of bullying in the aforementioned institutions, and al! acts of bullying by, among, and between the aforementioned persons shall be under the primary jurisdiction of the educational institution concerned.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: ACTS OF BULLYING IN THE WORKPI-ACE. Acts of bullying in the workplace can be defined as the intentiona! and repeated less favorable treatment of a person by another or others in the workplace, which may be considered unreasonable and inappropriate workplace practice, but excludes acts which necessarily fall under management prerogative and discipline done in good faith and without violating employee rights. Management prerogative here refers to the employer's inherent right to regulate, according to his own discretion and judgment, all aspects of employment, including hiring, work assignments, working methods, the time, place and manner of work, work supervision, transfer of employees, lay-off of workers, discipline, dismissal, and recall of employees. Ord. No. 0L92-23 Workplace bullying includes, but is not limited to, behavior that intimidates, offends, degrades or humiliates a worker, possibly in front of co-workers, clients, customers, vendors, visitors, and other persons in a workplace setting or outside therof, by reason of such employment. Acts of bullying in the workplace include the acts previously enumerated under and other acts such as, but not limited to: a. Frequently intimidating or undermining employees by demeaning their work standards, not giving them credit, setting them up for failure, and reminding them of old mistakes; b. Uninterrupted threatening of employees' personal self-esteem and work status; c. Continuous isolation of employees from opportunities, information, and interaction with others; d. Repeatedly giving impossible deadlines, creating undue pressure and stress, and overworking employees; e. Giving constant and unfair criticism; f. Persistent blaming without factual justification; g. Frequently making unreasonable demands; h. Giving hostile glares and other intimidating gestures repeatedly; i. Constant yelling, screaming, and swearing; j. Purposely excluding or isolating a coworker repeatedly; k. Frequently sending aggressive emails or notes; l. Incessant monopolization of supplies and other resources; m. Persistently engaging in excessive social bantering, teasing, and humiliation; n. Deliberately insulting others and taking paft in behind-the-back put-downs repeatedly; o. Monitoring another excessively in a continuous manner; p. Repeatedly stealing credit for other employees'work, except when the nature of the work is collective or commissioned.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: CYBERLIBEL - Cyberlibel is the unlawful or prohibited acts of libel as defined in Afticle 355 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended, committed through a computer system or any other similar means which may be devised in the future. Computer system refers to any device or group of interconnected or related devices, one or more of which, pursuant to a program, performs automated processing of data. It covers any type of device with data processing capabilities including, but not limited to, computers and mobile phones. The device consisting of hardware and software may include input, output and storage components which may stand alone or be connected in a network or other similar devices. It also includes computer data storage devices or media.
title: Ordinance No. 0192-23

text: ADDRESSING BULLYING IN EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIOilS -All educationa! institutions are hereby directed to adopt policies to address the existence of bullying. Such policies shall be regularly updated and, at a minimum, shall include provisions which: A.Identify the range of disciplinary administrative actions that may be taken against a respondent for bullying or retaliation which shall be commensurate with the nature and gravity of the offense: Provided, that, in addition to the disciplinary sanctions imposed upon a respondent of bullying or retaliation, he/she shall also be required to undergo a rehabilitation program which shall be administered by the institution concerned. The parents of the said respondent shall be encouraged by the said institution to join the rehabilitation program. 'i Page 5 of 10. O'rd. No. 0L92-23. B. Establish clear procedures and strategies for: 1. Reporting acts of bullying or retaliation; 2. Responding promptly to and investigating reports of bullying or retaliation; 3. Restoring a sense of safety for a victim and assessing the student's need for protection; 4. Protecting from bullying or retaliation of a person who reports acts of bullying, provides information during an investigation of bullying, or is witness to or has reliable information about an act of bullying; and 5. Providing counseling or referral to appropriate services for respondents, complainants, and appropriate family members of said students. C.Enable students to anonymously report bullying or retaliation: Provided, however, that no disciplinary administrative action shall be taken against a respondent solely on the basis of an anonymous report; D.Subject a student who knowingly makes a false accusation of bullying to disciplinary administrative action; E. Educate students on the dynamics of bullying, the anti-bullying policies of the school as well as the mechanisms of such school for the anonymous reporting of acts of bullying or retaliation; F. Educate parents and guardians about the dynamics of bullying, the anti-bullying policies of the school and how parents and guardians can provide support and reinfo

There are eight broad categories that create and sustain peaceful societies. The Institute of Economics and Peace has identified the following Eight (8) Pillars of Positive Peace as the most common characteristics of most peaceful societies. These pillars are the following: o well-functioning government; . low levels of corruption; o dcceptdnce ofthe rights ofothers; o good relations with neighbors; . sound business environment; . high levels of human capital; . equitable distribution of resources; and . free flow of information The concept of Positive Peace acknowledges that ending direct violence alone does not guarantee durable peace. Investing in Positive Peace improves resilience, mitigates risk of violence, and reduces the economic toll ftom conflict. text: Under SECTION 16, General Welfare Clause of the Loca! Government Code, Local Government Units are authorized to exercise the powers necessary, appropriate, or incidental to its efficient and effective governance and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare. Furthermore, under SECTION 2 of R.A. No. 10121, otherwise known as the Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010, the State aims to recognize the local risk patterns across the country, strengthen the capacity of LGUs for disaster risk reduction and management through decentralized powers, responsibilities, and resources at the regiona! and local levels, and strengthen the capacities of LGUs and communities in mitigating and preparing for, responding to, and recovering from the impact of disasters. Therefore, it is the declared policy of the City Government of Davao to protect the lives and propefties of its residents at all times, and, whenever possible, mitigate the effects of any man-made and natural disasters within its locality.

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS - As used in this Ordinance, the following terms are hereby defined: (a) Accredited Community Disaster Volunteerc (ACDV) - are individuals or organized volunteers who possess the requisite qualifications, as stipulated in the guidelines currently utilized by CDRRMO, and whose names were submitted as officially included in the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Counci! (CDRRMC), List of Community Disaster Volunteers, and/or the National Roster of ACDVs maintained by the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) and have the following roles: Provide voluntary seruice to Local Government Units and communities for DRRM-related activities. ii. Ensure that services rendered are done in a professional manner and does not compromise the safety of the volunteers and communities they are assisting. (b) Community Volunteer Responderc (CVR) - a group of responders in the community that pedorm response activities. (c) Disaster - a serious disruption of the functioning of a community or a society involving widespread human, material, economic or environmental losses and impacts, which exceeds the ability of the affected community or society to cope using its own resources. For purposes of this Ordinance, disaster shall include both natural calamities and man-made disasters. (d) Disaster Prevention - the outright avoidance of adverse impacts of hazards and other related disasters. Page 3 of L2 Ord. No. 0246-23 (e) Disaster Victims - persons or group of persons who have been adversely affected by a natural or human-induced hazard who have to leave their habitual places of residence due to existing or impending threats, damaged shelter units, with casualty among immediate family members or those who remained in their habitual places of origin when still habitable but whose main source of income or livelihood had been damaged and are experiencing hopelessness and difficulty in coping or responding to the onslaught of the hazardous events on their own resources. (f) Early Warning System (EWS) - refers to the set of capacities needed to generate and disseminate timely and meaningful warning information to enable individuals, communities, and organizations threatened by a hazard to prepare and act appropriately and insufficient time to reduce the possibility of harm or loss. (g) Emergency an unforeseen or sudden occurrence, especially danger, demanding an immediate action. (h) Emergency Evacuation means an evacuation ordered by competent authoriW when an unforeseen disaster has suddenly occurred which requires immediate evacuation of the affected area/s. (i) Evacuation - means an operation whereby all or part of a particular population is temporarily relocated, whether individually or in an organized manner, from an area in which a disaster or emergenry has been declared and which is considered dangerous to the health and safety of the general public. g) Evacuation Area, Evacuation Center, or Evacuation Place - a place where the Disaster Victims, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and Vulnerable and Marginalized Groups are brought before, during,and after calamities or disasters such as, but not limited to, typhoons, floods, landslides, eafthquakes or fire, for care, safety and protection. (k) Hazard - a dangerous phenomenon, substance, human activity, or condition that may cause loss of life, injury or other health impacts, propefi damage, loss of livelihood and services, social and economic disruption, or environmental damage. (l) Imminent Danger - means any condition in any place such that a danger exists which could reasonably be expected to cause death or serious physical harm immediately upon or before the occurrence of any human-induced or natural disasters. (m) Indigenous Early Warning System (IEWS) - a community's traditional way of giving Early Warning, such as batingaw and observing animal behavior, celestial bodies, etc., in determining possible weather disturbances. Whatever works for the barangay is acceptable as long as the meaning and the recommended action are properly disseminated to the community and constantly practiced through the conduct of drills and other skills enhancement exercises. (n) Internally Displaced Percon (IDP) or Percons Displaced by the Disaster (PDP) - refers to persons or groups of persons who have been forced or obliged to flee or to leave their homes or places of habitual residence, in pafticular as a result of or in order to avoid the effects of natural or human-induced disasters, and who have not crossed an internationally recognized State border. Page 4 of L2 Ord. No. 0246-23 (b) Preemptive Evacuation - means an evacuation ordered as a resoft when a disaster has been declared and danger or loss of life is imminent, and conditions exist that may critically imperi! or endanger the lives of those in a defined area. (p) Public Aleft and Warning System (PAWS) - a system used to give warning to the public, such as a Siren, to alert the public of impending disaster occurrence. PAWS is usually science-based technology and mostly, those that are state-of-the-art devices that have wider coverage in terms of monitoring and alerting, which benefits responsiveness to emergency management and public safety officials, and builds public trust, equity and confidence. (q) Recognized Volunteer Groups (RVG) - are volunteer groups not included under the definition of ACDVs but are recognized by the City Government of Davao or LDRRMC. (r) Reconstruction - the medium- and long-term rebuilding and sustainable restoration of resilient critical infrastructures, services, housing, facilities and livelihoods required for the ful! functioning of a community or a society affected by a disaster, aligning with the principles of sustainable development and "build back better," to avoid or reduce future disaster risk. (s) Recovery - the restoring or improving of livelihoods and health, as well as economic, physical, social, cultural and environmental assets, systems and activities, of a disaster-affected community or society, aligning with the principles of sustainable development and "build back betteri' to avoid or reduce future disaster risk. (t) Rehabilitation - the restoration of basic seruices and facilities for the functioning of a community or a society affected by a disaster. (u) Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) - a standard operating procedure is a set of step-by-step instructions compiled by an organization to help workers carry out routine operations. SOPs aim to achieve efficiency, quality output, and uniformity of peformance while reducing miscommunication and failure to comply with the organization's regulations. (v) Vulnerable Groups - include individuals or groups of people that face higher exposure to disaster risk and povefi including, but not limited to, women, especially pregnant and lactating mothers, children and youth, especially orphans and unaccompanied children, elderly, differently-abled people, and people with chronic illnesses.

text: LEGAL BASIS - SECTION 2l of Republic Act No. 10121 states that not less than five percent (5olo) of the estimated revenue from regular sources shall be set aside as Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (DLDRRMF) to suppoft disaster risk management activities such as, but not limited to, pre-disaster preparedness programs including training, purchasing life-saving rescue equipment, supplies and medicines, for post-disaster activities, and for the payment of premiums on calamity insurance. The same law likewise provides that, of the amount appropriated for LDRRMF, thity percent (30o/o) shall be allocated as Quick Response Fund (QRF) or stand-by fund for relief and recovery programs so that situation and living conditions of people in communities or areas stricken by disasters, calamities, epidemics, or complex emergencies, may be normalized as quickly as possible. Further, upon the recommendation of the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (LDRRMO) and approval of the sanggunian concerned, the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (LDRRMC) may transfer the said fund to support disaster risk reduction work of other LDRRMCs which are declared under the state of calamity.

text: LEGAL BASIS - SECTION 2l of Republic Act No. t072L states that not less than five percent (5olo) of the estimated revenue from regular sources shall be set aside as Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (LDRRMF) to suppoft disaster risk management activities such as, but not limited to, pre-disaster preparedness programs, including training, purchasing life-saving rescue equipment, supplies and medicines, for post-disaster activities, and for the payment of premiums on calamity insurance. The same law likewise provides that, of the amount appropriated for LDRRMF, thirty percent (30%) shall be allocated as Quick Response Fund (QRF) or stand-by fund for relief and recovery programs so that situations and living conditions of people in communities or areas stricken by disasters, calamities, epidemics, or complex emergencies, may be normalized as quickly as possible. Further, upon the recommendation of the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (LDRRMO) and approval of the sanggunian concerned, the Local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (LDRRMC) may transfer the said fund to support disaster risk reduction work of other LDRRMCs which are declared under a State of Calamity.
