text: - Pursuant to SECTION 2 of Republic Act No. 9729 or the "Climate Change Act of 2009" as amended by Republic Act No. L0174, the City Government of Davao hereby declares the following as its policies: 1. The Local Government shall afford full protection and advancement of the right of all Dabawenyos to a healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature; 2. The Local Government shall enjoin the pafticipation of national and local governments, businesses, non-government organizations, local communities and the public to prevent and reduce the adverse impacts of climate change and, at the same time, maximize the potential benefits of climate change; 3. It shall also be the policy of the Local Government to strengthen, integrate, consolidate and institutionalize government initiatives to achieve coordination in the implementation of plans and programs to address climate change in the context of sustainable development; 4. The Local Government recognizes that climate change and disaster risk reduction and management are closely interrelated and effective. Disaster risk reduction and management will enhance adaptive capacity to climate change. In consonance with this, the Local Government shall integrate disaster risk reduction into climate change programs and initiatives; 5. Finally, the Local Government shall embrace a systematic concept of climate change in various phases of policy formulation, development plans, povefi reduction strategies and other development tools and techniques by all agencies and instrumentalities of the government.

The city shall, therefore, assist in every way possible the solo parents in raising of their families and in providing their children a better future hoping that -such efforts will contribute greatly to the continued realization of a ,.child riiendly city".
title: AN ORDINANCE INSTITUTIONALIZING THE PROGRAMS, SERVICES, PRMLEGES, AND BENEFITS FOR SOLO PARENTS AND THEIR CHILDREN, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES PURSUANT TO REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8972, AS AMENDED By REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11861, KNOWN AS THE EXPANDED SOLO PARENTS WELFARE ACT

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS. For purposes of this Ordinance and pursuant to Republic Act No. 8972, as amended by Republic Act No. 11861, the following terms shall mean: a) Solo Parents - refer to unmarried, separated, annulled, widower and widowed individuals, and any person, whether male or female, falling under the enumeration provided under SECTION 4, Republic Act No. 11861 and its Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR), who have taken the sole responsibility of parenthood. 1. A woman who got pregnant as a result of rape and other crimes against chastity even without a final conviction of the offender: Provided, That the mother keeps and raises the child; 2. A widow left solo or alone to take responsibility for the children; 3. A person who has a spouse left solo or alone with the responsibility of parenthood while the spouse is detained or is seruing sentence for a criminal conviction for at least three (3) months; 4. A person left solo or alone with the responsibility of parenthood due to physical and/or mental incapacity of spouse as certified by a public medical practitioner; 5. Parent left solo or alone with the responsibility of parenthood due to legal separation or de facto separation from spouse for at least six (6) months; 6. Parent left solo or alone with the responsibility of parenthood due to declaration of nullity or annulment of marriage as decreed by a court; 7. Any other person who solely provides parental care and suppoft to a child or children; B. Abandonment by the spouse for at least six (6) months; 9. spouse or any family member of an overseas Filipino worker (oFW), or the guardian of the child or children of an oFW: provided, That the said oFW belongs to the low/semi-skilled worker category and is away from the Philippines for an uninterrupted period of twelve (12) months: Provided, fufther, that the oFW, his or her spouse, family member, or guardian of the child or children of an oFW falls under the requirements of Republic Act No. 11861; Page 3 0f 12 ord. Ni 0393-24 10. Unmarried mother or father who keeps and rears the child or children; 11. Any legal guardian, adoptive or foster parent who solely provides parental care and support to a child or children; 12. Any relative within fourth (4th) civil degree of consanguinity or affinity of the parent or legal guardian who assumes parental care and suppoft of the child or children as a result of the death, abandonment, disappearance or absence of the parents or solo parent for at least six (6) months: Provided, That in cases of solo grandparents who are senior citizens but who have the sole parenta! care and support over their grandchildren who are unmarried, or unemployed and twenty-two (22) years old or below, or those twentytwo (22) years old or over but who are unable to fully take care or protect themselves from abuse, neglect, cruelty, exploitation, or discrimination because of a physical or mental disability or condition; 13. A pregnant woman who provides sole parental care and support to the unborn child or children.; b) Abandonment - refers to the absence by one spouse, followed by prolonged absence without just cause; c) Children or dependents - refer to those living with and dependent upon the solo parent for suppoft who are unmarried, unemployed and twenty-two (22) years old or below, or those over twenty-two (22) years old but who are unable to fully take care or protect themselves from abuse, neglect, cruelty, exploitation, or discrimination because of a physical or mental disability or condition; Provided, that children or dependent/s entitled to be suppofted beyond the age of majority shall be limited to those who are in school or in training for some profession, trade or vocation, consistent with and as provided in Afticle 194 of Executive Order No. 209 (E.O. No. 209), or The Family Code of the Philippines; Provided, fufther, That this definition shall only apply for purposes of availing of the benefits under this Act"; d) Parental Responsibility - with respect to their minor child, shall refer to the rights and duties of the parents as deflned in Afticle 220 of Executive Order No. 209, as amended, otherwise known as the "Family Code of the Philippines"; e) Flexible Work Schedule - refers to a work arrangement granted to solo parent employees to vary the arrival time and depafture in the workplace without affecting the core work hours as defined by the employer; f) Parental Leave - refers to leave benefits granted to a solo parent to enable the performance of parental duties and responsibilities where physical presence is required or beneficial to the child; g) Basic Necessities - are goods vital to the needs of consumers for their sustenance and existence. For purposes of this Ordinance, basic necessities shall include: I Page 4 of L2 ord. No. 0393-24 1. All kinds and variants of rice; 2. Corn; 3. All kinds of bread excluding cakes and other kinds of pastries; 4. Bath soap; 5. Alcohol; 6. Fresh, dried and canned fish, and other marine products including those frozen and in various modes of packaging; 7. Fresh pork, beef and poultry meat; 8. All kinds of fresh eggs except quai! eggs; 9. Potable water in bottles and containers; 10. Fresh and processed milk including milk labeled as food supplement; 11. Fresh vegetables including root crops; 12. Fresh fruits; 13. Locally manufactured instant noodles; 14. Coffee and coffee creamer; 15. All kinds of sugar except sweeteners; 16. All kinds of cooking oil; 17. Salt; 18. Powdered, Iiquid or bar laundry and detergent soap; 19. Household Liquefied Petroleum Gas, not more than 11 kgs. LpG content once every five (5) months bought from LpG dealers; and 20. Kerosene, not more than 2 liters per month; h) Infant and Child Rearing Necessities - are those which are vital to the needs of infants, and children under six (6) years of age. These items are, but not limited, to the following: 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. text: DECLARATION OF POLICY - The State shall take measures, with the participation of the Indigenous Cultural Communities/Indigenous Peoples (ICCs/IPs) and Muslim Cultural Tribes concerned, to protect their rights and guarantee respect for their cultural integrity, and to ensure that members of the ICCs/IPs benefit on an equal footing from the rights and oppoftunities which national laws and regulations grant to other members of the population. The State also recognizes its obligations to respond to the strong expression of the ICCs/IPs for cultural integrity by assuring maximum ICC/IP participation in the direction of education, health, as well as other seruices of ICCs/IPs, in order to render such seruices more responsive to the needs and desires of these communites.

text: SIElgre - Qualified Indigenous Peoples (IPs) and Muslim tribe beneficiaries residing in far-flung areas of Davao City may avail of the seruices offered by the Ordinance. In establishing an operationa! inpatient shelter facility for Indigenous Peoples and Muslims (IPs/Muslims), the following are considerable objectives to prioritize the well-being, cultural sensitivity, and specific needs of this community: 1. Ensure that the facility respects and incorporates Indigenous cultural practices, traditions, and languages to create a culturally safe and welcoming environment; 2. Provide access to healthcare seruices that are sensitive to the unique health challenges faced by Indigenous Cultural Communities (ICCs), including addressing issues related to historical trauma and disparities in healthcare access by offering a range of seruices that address not only physical health but also mental, emotional, and spiritual wellbeing, reflecting indigenous concepts of holistic health; 3. Implement trauma-informed care principles to create a safe and suppottive environment for Indigenous and Muslim individuals who may have experienced historical or personal trauma by providing counselling seruices that is culturally relevant to the individuals seeking help; 4. Involve Indigenous and Muslim community members in the planning, operation, and decision-making processes to ensure that the facility meets their specific needs and preferences; 5. Collaborate with Indigenous and Muslim-led organizations and tribal authorities to strengthen the network of support and resources available to the community; 6. Ensure that the facility's physical environment, design, and artwork are culturally appropriate and reflect Indigenous and Muslim aesthetics and values; Ord. No. 0429-24 7. Develop a sustainable operational and funding plan that ensures the facility's long-term existence and effectiveness in meeting the needs of Indigenous and Muslim individuals; and 8. To supplement other government seruices to the eleven (11) major tribes not mentioned in this Ordinance.

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS - As used in this Ordinance, the following terms and phrases shall mean as follows: 1. City Government - refers to the City Government of Davao. 2. Geodiversity - the natural range or diversity of geological features (rocks, minerals, fossils, structures), geomorphological features (landforms and processes), soil and water that compose and shape the physical landscape. It is not usually defined to inctude landscaping, concrete, or other human landforms and products. 3. Geological heritage (geoheritage) - a generic but descriptive term applied to sites or areas of geologic features with significant scientific, educational, cultural, or aesthetic value. Ord. No. 0464-24 4. Geoparks- are places where landscapes with outstanding geological heritage are used to suppoft sustainable development. This is achieved through conseryation, education, inlerpersonal and naturebased tourism. 5. National Integrated Protected Areas System (NIPAS) the classification and administration of all designated protected areas to maintain essential ecological processes and life-support systems, to preserue genetic diversity, to ensure sustainable use of resources found therein, and to maintain their natural conditions to the greatest extend possible. 6. Natural park - a relatively large area not materially altered by human activity where extractive resources uses are not allowed and is maintained to protect outstanding natural and scenic areas of national or international significance for scientific, educational, and recreational use. 7. Protected area - identified portions of land and/or water set aside by reason of their unique physical and biological diversity and protected against destructive human exploitation. 8. UNESCO Global Geoparks (UGGp) - single, unified geographical areas where sites and landscapes of internationa! geological significance are managed with a holistic concept of protection, education and sustaina ble development. sEcTroN 5. MANAGEMENT oF MOUNT APo GEOPARK - The Mount Apo Geopark shall be managed pursuant to Republic Act 11038 and Republic Act 9237 or the Mount Apo Act of 2003. UNESCO Global Geoparks are managed by a Body having legal existence recognized under national legislation. This management body should be appropriately equipped to address the entire area and should include all relevant local and regional actors and authorities. UNESCO Global Geoparks require a management plan, agreed upon by all the paftners, that provides for the social and economic needs of the local populations, protects the landscape in which they live and conserues their cultural identity. The plan must be comprehensive, incorporating the governance, development, communication, protection, infrastructure, finances and partnerships of the UNESCO Global Geopark. DENR Region XI shall be the primary agency to manage the Mount Apo Geopark (Davao City side), in close coordination with the Loca! Government Unit (LGU)-Davao City and other concerned organizations/groups. The Regional Director may enter into a Memorandum of Agreement (MoA)/Partnership Agreement with the concerned LGU, and peoples Organizations.

text: TITLE - This Ordinance shall be known as *THE REVISED COMPREHENSIVE ANTI-SMOKING ORDINANCE OF DAVAO CIW'.
title: Ordinance No. 0472-24

text: DECIARATION OF POUCY- Pursuant to Republic Act (R.A.) No. 7160 (Local Government Code of 1991), the City Government of Davao shall exercise the powers expressly granted, those necessarily implied therefrom, as well as powers necessary, appropriate, or incidental for its efficient and effective governance, and those which are essential to the promotion of the general welfare. Within its respective territorial jurisdiction, it shall ensure and support the maintenance of peace and order, and the preseruation of the comfort and convenience of its inhabitants. Thus, it is the Poliry of the City Government of Davao to ensure the prevention, suppression, and imposition of proper penalties for smoking, vaping, or engaging in similar activities in public places, selling the same to minors or allowing them to engage in such activities and such other acts using the same that are inimica! to the heatth and welfare of the inhabitants of the City.
title: Ordinance No. 0472-24

text: DEFINITION OF TERMS - For purposes of this Ordinance, the following terms are defined operationally: 1. Accommodation and Enteftainment Establishments - refer to establishments that provide food, accommodation, drinks, merchandise, entertainment or other professional seruices, including but not limited to, restaurants, fast foods, eateries, hotels, motels, lodges, inns, boarding houses, disco houses, videoke bars, resto bars, and movie houses, or any other place with pleasant environment and atmosphere conducive to comfoft, healthful relaxation and rest, offering food and/or drinks, sleeping accommodation and recreation facilities to the public for a fee; 2. Centers of Youth Activities - refer to places such as playschools, preparatory schools, elementary schools, high schools, colleges and universities, youth hostels, parks and playgrounds, and other recreational facilities for minors; 3. Children Rescued - refer to minors rescued from any conceivable forms of danger, including substance use and abuse; 4. Electronic Device Systems (EDS) - refer to any device, such as electronic nicotine device system, electronic cigarette, vapes and other similar devices, whether or not it is used to deliver nicotine to the user, that resembles the outward appearance of real smoking products; 5. Enclosed or Paftially Enclosed Public Place - refers to all places, which are enclosed by one or more walls or sides, whether covered by a roof or not, or even if open on all sides but is covered by a roof, regardless of whether the structure is permanent or temporary in nature, that are accessible or open to the public, whether or not by invitation or by payment, or all places for collective use, regardless of ownership or right to access including, but not limited to, gasoline stations, banks, malls, shopping/business arcades, town squares, terminals, airpoft, seaports, schools, places of worship/churches, hospitals, cinema houses, gymnasiums/covered courts, funeral parlors, barber shops, cockpits, gaming Page 3 of t4 Ord. No. 0472-24 areas, recreational facilities, pedestrian overpass, indoor car parks, waiting sheds, sidewalks, and other places where people usually congregate; 6. Immediately Dangerous to Life or Health (IDLH) - describes hazards in which an acute exposure to the hazard poses a severe risk of immediate health damage, injury, or death. This is determined by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) or the City Health Office (CHO), with proper coordination with the FDA, in accordance with their existing policies and standards; 7. Minors - are persons who are below the age of majority or below the legal age of eighteen (18) years, or persons who are eighteen (18) years of age or older, but are incapable of taking care of themselves due to their mental incapacity; 8. Person-in-charge - refers to the president/manager, in case of a company, corporation, paftnership or association, the owner/proprietor/operator, in case of a single proprietorship, of accommodation and entertainment establishments, whether tourism-accredited or not, or the administrator in case of government or private propefi, facility, office or building, workplaces, enclosed or paftially enclosed public places, public buildings, public outdoor spaces, places of worship, hazardous areas, food preparation areas, health facilities of any kind, centers of youth activity or other facilities frequented particularly by minors, and the city/municipal schools superintendent, school president, dean or principal, in case of schools; 9. Public Conveyances - refer to any vehicle, whether mobile or stationary, used in the transpoft of passengers or available to the public as a mode of transport, such ds, but not limited to, jeepneys, buses, trains, vans, taxis, airplanes, ships, and other modes of water transpoftation, trirycles, motorcycles, and other public utility vehicles whether covered by a Certiflcate of Public Convenience or not; 10. Public Building - refers to any of the following: A building or structure owned by the government or owned by a private person but used, rented, or occupied by the government or any of its instrumentalities; or Any building or structure used or controlled exclusively for public purposes by any depaftment or branch of government, local government unit, or barangay without reference to the ownership of the building; 11. Public Outdoor Spaces - refer to outdoor spaces that are open to the public or places where facilities are available for the public or where a crowd of people gather or congregate or regardless of ownership or right to access such as, but not limited to, parks, playgrounds, spofts grounds or centers, gaming areas, gardens, resorts, beaches, pools, markets, streets, sidewalks, parking areas, walkways, entrance ways, waiting areas, stairwells and the like' 12. Shisha - refers to a device or instrument which may have a single or multistemmed pipe for smoking, whether or not it delivers nicotine to the user, in which the smoke is passed through a water basin before inhalation. It is also known as water pipe, Sheesha, Hookah, Nergeela, Argeel and Nargile; a I Page 4 of L4 Ord. No. 0472-24 13. Smoking/Vaping - refers to the lighting and/or puffing of any cigarette, cigar, tobacco product of any kind, form or type, EDS, Shisha, vape and the like, whether it contains nicotine or not. Possession of any lighted and/or puffed cigarette, cigar or any tobacco product, or an actually operated EDS, Shisha, Vape and the like within the prohibited areas for smoking shall constitute "prima facid'evidence of smoking/vaping as prohibited under this ordinance; 14. Tobacco Product - any product that consists of loose tobacco, whether or not it contains nicotine, and is intended for use in a cigarette, including any product containing tobacco, and intended for smoking/vaping or oral or nasal use; and 15. workplaces - an area, permanent or temporary, in which a person performs duties of employment or work, regardless of whether the work is done for compensation or on a voluntary basis, and includes private offices, common area and any other area which is generally used or frequented during the course of employment or work. Company-owned vehicles used for transpofting employees and guests or any vehicle used in the course of work are considered workplaces.
title: Ordinance No. 0472-24

text: COVERAGE - It shall be unlawful for any person to smoke/vape or allow the smoking/vaping of any tobacco product, or use EDS, Shisha, Vape and the like, in all forms of Public Conveyances, Government-owned Vehicles, Accommodation and Enteftainment Establishments, Workplaces, Enclosed or Partially Enclosed Public Places, Public Buildings and Public Outdoor Spaces, Places of Worship, Hazardous Areas, Food Preparation Areas, Health Facilities of any kind, Centers of Youth Activities, and areas within one hundred (100) meters from any point of the perimeter of Schoots, Public Playgrounds or other facilities frequented particularly by minors, except in duly designated smoking/vaping areas as deflned in SECTION 5 hereunder, within the territorial jurisdiction of Davao City. It shall also be unlawful for any person to domestically manufacture or adulterate any tobacco product, EDS, Shisha, Vape and the like that are IDLH. It shall also be unlawful for any person, natural or juridical, to direct, order, compel, request or ask a minor to acquire or purchase from, possess, sell, offer or distribute any tobacco product, EDS, Shisha, Vape and the like, to any other person and/or for any other person, and to allow, abet, tolerate or permit such minor to acquire, purchase, possess, sell, offer, distribute, use, consume, or smoke/vape any tobacco product, EDS, Shisha, Vape, and the like.

text: DESIGNATED SMOKING/VAPING AREA (DSVA) - refers to an outdoor space where a person is permitted to smoke and vape without violating this Ordinance, provided that, the same meets the following requirements, at the minimum: There shall be no opening that will allow air to escape from the DSVA to the smoke/vape-free area of the building or conveyance, except for a single door equipped with an automatic door closer; It shall be located in or within ten (10) meters from entrances, exits, or any place where people pass or congregate, or in front of air intake ducts; Page 5 of t4 Ord. No. 0472-24 The DSVA shall not be larger than twenty percent (20o/o) of the total floor area of the building or conveyance, provided that, in no case shall such area be larger than five (5) square meters; No building or conveyance shall have more than one DSVA; Provided that, persons-in-charge have the option of establishing one (1) Designated Smoking Area (DSA) and one (1) Designated Vaping Area (DVA) therein, subject to the same standards under this SECTION, with a combined area not exceeding twenty percent (20o/o) of the total floor area of the building or conveyance; Minors shall not be allowed inside the DSVA; It shall have the following signages highly visible and prominently displayed: a. "Smoking/Vaping Area" signage; b. Graphic health warnings on the effects of using tobacco products, EDS, Shisha, Vape and the like; and c. text: PROHIBITION ON THE SELLING, SERVING, PROVIDING AND OFFERING OF LIOUOR AND OTHER ATCOHOLIC BEVERAGES TO MINORS.- A. No person or establishment may sell, selve, provide, or offer Iiquor, alcoholic beverages, coconut wine or tuba, and other locally distitled alcoholic drinks to minors. Likewise, it shal! be unlawful for any person to practice, or establishment to allow the "tagay system" or sharing of glasses and to have a drinking session with minors, regardless of the relationship of the minor to the person with them. B. When the age of a person to be served is in doubt, the owners, managers, or employees of said establishments are mandated to require the presentation of such person's valid government-issued identification (ID) card, which shall be "prima facie" evidence of the age of said persons. a. Persons who fail to show their valid government-issued ID cards or who present such ID which is of questionable validity shall be denied seruice. In the case of minors, he/she shall be immediately referred to the City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO) for his/her rescue. The children rescued under this Ordinance shall be subjected to and dealt with following the provisions of the Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act of 2006 under R.A. No. 9344, as amended by R.A. No. 10630, and the chitd and Youth welfare code of L974, under Presidential Decree (p.D) No. 603. b. Persons or establishments who fail to require the presentation of such valid government-issued ID cards shall be held liable under SECTION 15 of this Ordinance. c. It shall not be a defense for any person, or establishment and its employees in selling, serving, providing, or offering any liquor and other alcoholic beverages, that he/she/it did not know or was not aware of the real age of the minor. Neither shall it be a defense that he/she/it did not know nor had any reason to believe that any liquor and alcoholic beverages were for the utilization or consumption of the minor to whom it was sold. C. Persons who acquire, buy, purchase or possess liquor and other atcoholic beverages on behalf of a minor, or direct, order, compel, request, ask, force, abet, or permit a minor to acquire, buy, purchase, possess, use or consuffle liquor and other alcoholic beverages shall be accordingly penalized under this Ordinance. text: DECLARATION OF POUCY - Pursuant to SECTION 16 of Republic Act No. 7t60, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991", the City Government of Davao shall exercise the powers expressly granted, those necessarily implied therefrom, as well as powers necessary, appropriate or incidental for its efficient and effective governance, and those which are essential to the promotion of general welfare; and shall ensure and suppoft preseruation and enrichment of culture, promote safety, improve public morals, enhance social justice, maintain peace and order and preserve the comfoft and convenience of their inhabitants. Republic Act No. 10533 - otherwise known as "An Act Enhancing the Philippine Basic Education System by Strengthening its Curriculum and Increasing the Number of Years for Basic Education and Appropriating Funds Therefor and Other Purposes" in SECTION 5. (h) Curriculum Development states that "The DepEd shall formulate the design and details of the enhanced basic education curriculum. The curriculum shall be flexible enough to enable and allow schools to localize, indigenize and enhance the same based on their respective educational and social contexts. The production and development of locally produced teaching materials shall be encouraged and approval of these materials shall devolve to the regional and division education units". Likewise, the City Government of Davao aims to ensure that the people of Davao are empowered, protected, secure, gender and culturally sensitive to attain the best quality of life. Davao City aims to cultivate a disciplined and law-abiding citizenry, starting from the youngest member of society.

text: OBJECTIVES The objectives of this Ordinance are as follows: a. To develop among children and the youth an authentic appreciation of their sense of moral responsibility to their fellow citizens, democratic institutions, and human society. b. To empower the children and youth as future adults for them to understand, protect and help promote the common good as law-abiding citizens through self-discipline. c. To enable the children and youth to understand, reflect, and fully discern the role that social media and modern technology play in their lives. d. To guide the children and youth in realizing their duties as stewards of the environment and the good of the future generation. e. To form the children and youth into individuals who do not discriminate against others, especially the poor, and respect women, the elderly, Indigenous Peoples and the LGBTQ community. Ord. Justice Zone Convenor - A representative of a justice sector agency who leads the Justice Zone administratively in the planning and implementation of Justice Zone programs and projects. text: POLICY FORMUIATION - The Davao City Justice Zone shall formulate measures aimed at improving the delivery of just, responsive, and accountable justice services in the city. Such measures may be raised for consideration of the Sanggunian, for appropriate local legislation and budgets or to the Justice Sector Coordinating Counci! (JSCC). Al! such measures must conform and not contravene the policy directives set forth by JSCC, the policies of the member institutions, and existing laws and regulations.
title: Ordinance No. 0624-24

text: PIANNING AND PROGRAMMING - In accordance with policy directions and resolutions of the JSCC, the Davao City Justice Zone shall prepare plans, programs, and services with accompanying budgets aimed at operationalizing measures to improve the delivery of just, responsive, and accountable justice services in the city. Measures within the purview of the Davao City Justice Zone are, but not limited to, the following: a. Davao City Swift Justice Program to improve efficiency in the administration of justice, addressing issues in the justice system, such as clogged dockets, and ensuring that all pillars of the justice qystem work together to promote justice by disposing cases expeditiously; b. Improving access to justice of the poor and marginalized, especially women, children, indigenous peoples, people of diverse sexual orientation and gender identity and expression (SOGIE), among others; c. Enabling the barangay justice system, as well as customary and traditional justice systems to uphold rights-based approaches and build links with the formal justice mechanisms; and d. Rehabilitation and reintegration of Persons Deprived of Libefi (PDL) into society, among others. Page Ord. 5of7 No. 0624-24 The City Justice Zone Plan will form part of the city's local development plan, such as, the Comprehensive Development Plan (CDP) and its Annual Investment Plan (AIP), to ensure that it has appropriate political and financial resources for implementation. It shall be formulated alongside the local development planning process of the city, which shall be reviewed every three (3) years and updated annually. It shall be formulated based on the assessment of the justice issues and needs of the city, and in cognizance with national plans, such as, the Philippine Development Plan. Resources for the implementation of the plan could be sourced from the local budget and the convergence budget of JSCC. External fund sourcing may be undertaken, but with the concurrence of the members of the Davao City Justice Zone. SECTION.3.@-TheDavaoCityJusticeZoneshal|coordinate with relevant agencies, offices, and organizations to support the delivery of just, responsive, and accountable justice seruices in the city. It shall initiate referral pathways to link individuals as well as groups to services related to access to justice, such as, health, psychosocial support, case management, safety and security, among others. The Davao City Justice Zone may formulate Memoranda of Understanding (MOU) with specific institutions and organizations to create partnerships and strengthen justice service delivery subject to the approval of the JSCC Principals. It may also formulate policies, projects, and seruices as a result of coordination work within and among justice zone members and other justice actors.
title: Ordinance No. 0624-24

text: UQNIIQBING - The Davao City Justice Zone shall utilize its regular meetings to monitor progress of measures as identified in ib plan and agreements made in view of improving the delivery of just, responsive, and accountable justice seruices in the city. It shall harvest lessons learned in implementing justice-related policies, plans, programs and seruices, and good practices. It shall develop annual reports to be submitted to the Sanggunian and the Mayor, and to JSCC containing accomplishments towards benchmarking best practices on Justice delivery as well as recommendations to improve the delivery of justice in the city. text: Sexually Transmitted Infections, Human Immunodeficienry Virus and Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (STIs, HIV and AIDS) are public health concerns that have wide ranging social, political and economic repercussions, as such: 1. The City of Davao shall establish policies and programs to prevent the spread of STI, HIV and AIDS and deliver treatment, care and support seruices to persons living with HIV (PLHIV) and those with Sexually Transmitted Infections (5[s) in accordance with evidence-based strategies and approaches that follow the principles of human rights, gender equality, and meaningful pafticipation of communities affected by the epidemic; 2. The City Government of Davao shall adopt a multi-sectoral and culturallysensitive approach in responding to the STI, HIV and AIDS epidemic by ensuring that local communities, civil society groups, and persons living with HIV and their families are paft of the response to the epidemic; 3. The City Government of Davao shall ensure that STIs, HIV and AlDS-related services are accessible, available, affordable, and acceptable to those who need them. It shall also implement policies, programs, projects and activities that will contribute to eliminating stigma and discrimination; 4. The City Government of Davao shall consciously adhere to generally-accepted principles of human rights and adopt gender perspectives in dealing with STIs, HIV and AIDS, as it shall employ scientifically-proven approaches in its information and education campaigns; Further, the City of Davao affirms that: 1. The protection, promotion and fulfillment of human rights as the cornerstone of an effective response to the epidemic; 2. The meaningful inclusion and participation of persons directly and indirectly affected by the epidemic, especially persons living with HIV is crucial in eliminating the virus; 3. Unless otherwise provided in this Ordinance, the confidentiality, anonymity and non-compulsory nature of HIV testing and HlV-related testing shall always be guaranteed and protected by the City Government of Davao; and 4. Policies and practices that discriminate on the basis of perceived or actual HIV status, sex, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, economic status, ethnicity and disability are inimical to national interest and contrary to the rights and freedoms guaranteed in the Constitution, and the City Government of Davao shall eliminate these acts of discrimination. text: - It is the policy of Davao City to recognize and celebrate the cultural and spiritual heritage of its people. In support of this commitment, Davao City hereby declares the month of January as Bible Month, an annual obseruance promoting the teachings, values, and wisdom of the Bible as paft of Davao's cultural and moral development.

text: @IElgre - The objectives of this Ordinance are as follows: a) To encourage reflection on the teachings of the Bible and its relevance in promoting peace, unity, and moral integrity in Davao City; b) To promote intefaith understanding and respect for religious diversity within the City; and c) To inspire community engagement through organized activities that honor the Bible and encourage values formation across all sectors.

text: BIBLE MONTH ACTMTIES - During the Bible Month, the following activities are encouraged across Davao City: 1. The City Government, in paftnership with the private sector, Biblebelieving institutions/organizations, and NGOs, shall coordinate citywide events such as Bible exhibits, poster-making contests, seminars, and reflections that promote unity, moral values and other activities; 3. All Barangay Councils in Davao City are encouraged to suppoft and participate in Bible Month activities to foster a spirit of community, love and seruice.
title: AN ORDINANCE INSTITUTING JANUARY AS BIBLE MONTH IN DAVAO CITY

text: - The implementation of this Ordinance shall be under the Office of the City Mayor through the Moral Recovery Council, in coordination with the National Bible Month Ecumenical Team. text: - The following are hereby declared policies of the City: a. To promote, improve, and safeguard the Panigan-Tamugan Watershed as the main suface water source of the City's drinking water and is the largest source of the City's suface water supply; b. To effectively manage and protect the physical, biological, and socio-economic attributes of the Panigan-Tamugan Watershed based on the assessment study based on the masterplan as specified under SECTION 4 therein; c. To ensure the Panigan-Tamugan Watershed's cleanliness, sustainable ecological balance, rich biodiversity, and improve the quality of life of the community; and d. To recognize that the watershed area is a recharged area for the City's aquifers which are sources of the City's drinking water that must be protected, conserved, maintained, and managed for the continued and full enjoyment of the present and future generations. sEcTIoN3.rc.Forthepurposeofthisordinance,the following terms are defined as follows: a. "Critical Waterched" pertains to areas of land which show critical degradation as to threaten their natural feature on which rainwater drains from a river system to a common outlet such as a dam, lake or sea; or areas where rain from a higher level of land flows down to a river, or stream then to the Davao Gulf; or a topographically delineated area of land from which rainwater can drain as sufface run-off via a specific river or stream system to a common outlet point, which may be a dam, irrigation system or a municipal water supply take-off point, or where a river or stream discharges water into a larger river, stream or lake. b. "Customaty Laws" refer to a body of written and/or unwritten rules, usages, customs and practices traditionally and continually recognized, accepted and observed by respective ICCs/IPs; c. "Environmentally Critical Areas (ECA)" refer to those areas declared by law as nationa! parks, watershed reserves, wildlife preserves and sanctuaries and all other areas identified as such by Presidential Proclamation 2L46, specifically in Items B, 1-11. d. "Groundwater" refers to subsurface water that occurs beneath a water table in soils and rocks, or in geological formations. e. "Indigenous Cultural Communities/Indigenous Peoples (ICCs llPs)' refer to groups of people or homogenous societies identified under Republic Act No. 837L, or The Indigenous Peoples Rights Act (IPRA) of L99T" generally consisting of the Obu Manuvu and other tribes within the PTW. Page 3 of I Ord. No, 0742-25 t. "Motorized equipment" refers to any machine that uses or is activated by a motor, engine, or other power source. For the purpose of this Ordinance, motorized equipment shall refer to chainsaws, drilling machines, sawmills or pumping stations. g. "Open dump" refers to a disposal area wherein the solid wastes are indiscriminately thrown or disposed of without due planning and consideration for environmental and health standards (R.A. No. 9003). h. "Protected Areas" refer to identified portions of land and water set aside by reasons of their unique physical and biological significance, managed to enhance biological diversity and protected against destructive human exploitation. i. 'PUSAI(A" is the traditiona! Obu Manuvu practice of sanctiffing entities, living or non-living, as "precious" or "sacred" because it has become priceless, from the perspective of a family, clan, or tribe. j. "Settlement" refers to formal and informal communities or built-up residential areas where people prefer to live in and land areas classified, zoned or convefted for current or future residential or housing development purposes, including socialized housing zones for the homeless and underprivileged. k. "Suface Water" refers to waters (e.9., rivers, lakes, bays) which are open to the atmosphere and subject to surface runoff. l. "Tourism and Recreational Activities" refer to activities people do for fun and enjoyment which shal! refer to trekking or hiking, swimming, camping, mountain biking, running, canoeing, kayaking, rafting, tubing, for recreational purposes. m. *Waterched Areas" are areas of land which rainwater drains via a river system to a common outlet such as dam, lake or the sea; an area where rain from the highest point flows down to a river and ultimately to the Davao Gulf or a topographical delineated area of land from which rainwater can drain as suface run-off via a specific stream of river system to a common outlet point which may be a dam, irrigation system or municipal water supply take-off point, or where the stream or river discharges water into a larger river, stream or lake. n. "Watershed Management" is the process of guiding and organizing uses of Iand and other resources in a watershed to provide desired goals and services without adversely affecting the watershed areas and water resources. o. 'Watershed Management Council (WMC)" refers to a Body which issues policies and guidelines and sets the direction of collaboration in gathering, processing and evaluating information on watershed areas in Davao City and develops plans and strategies towards ensuring its health and sustainability.
